target.title: test: serialize Vitest mock resolution in isolate:false shared workers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`subagent-orphan-recovery` tests flaked on main (run 29566318167): two tests received the bare interrupted-task resume template instead of the mocked transcript content — the `vi.mock` factory's configured return never reached prod code.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause is an upstream Vitest 4 mocker re-entrancy hole our isolate:false shared workers expose: `BareModuleMocker.resolveMocks()` has no in-flight guard — it snapshots `pendingIds`, resolves ids via parallel `resolveId` RPCs, re-registers each manual mock (invalidating the mock module node), and only then clears the queue. Leaked real-timer async work from an earlier shard file can start a **second concurrent resolveMocks pass** over the same ids; the slower pass invalidates the already-evaluated mock module mid-import-chain, so importers evaluated before the wipe hold factory instance A while later importers re-run the factory and get instance B — the test configures A, prod reads B's default (`[]`), and the resume prompt loses its transcript sections. `vi.hoisted`-stable mocks are immune, matching the CI signature test-for-test.

Fix at the runner ownership boundary (`test/non-isolated-runner.ts`): `onCollectStart` installs a per-worker `serializeMockerResolveMocks` — concurrent callers coalesce into one shared drain, and ids pushed into the abandoned snapshot during a pass's RPC window are requeued and drained before any awaiting import proceeds. Registration + invalidation happen exactly once, before evaluation. This hardens every isolate:false shard, not just the flaking file.

Upstream note: this is a genuine `@vitest/mocker` bug worth filing against vitest 4 (`resolveMocks` re-entrancy).

## User Impact

None at runtime — test-runner infrastructure only.

## Evidence

- Deterministic repro (poison file with a 1ms recurring dynamic-import timer + `resolveId` jitter): reproduces the exact CI failures (same 2 tests, same lines, same received text) on the unfixed runner; 5/5 green with the fix; A/B verified both directions.
- Stress: 10× the target file and 5× the full agentic-agents-core-subagents set (63 files, 1220 tests) at OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=6 — all green; exact-CI-order and shuffled-seed runs green.
- New behavioral tests in test/non-isolated-runner.resolve-mocks.test.ts (coalescing, late-queue requeue, idempotent install, fresh pass).
- Lint/format/check:test-types clean; autoreview round 1 raised one accepted P2 (pure coalescing would drop late-queued ids) — fixed with the requeue commit; final review clean ("patch is correct 0.91").

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `parseJsonWithJson5Fallback()` silently discards the `JSON.parse` error when both `JSON.parse` and `JSON5.parse` fail. Callers currently lose the stricter JSON diagnostic context and only receive the JSON5 error, making it harder to debug why valid JSON was rejected.

The function now catches both errors explicitly, includes the JSON parse error message in the rethrown `Error`, and preserves the JSON5 error as `Error.cause`. The fast path (strict JSON succeeds) and JSON5 fallback (single parser fails) are unchanged.

## User Impact

Callers can extract both the JSON diagnostic and the JSON5 cause from the error chain, enabling better debugging without bypassing caller-owned sanitization. Config loading with malformed files now produces richer error diagnostics.

target.title: fix(proxy): guard JSON.parse in proxy error response parsing

## What Problem This Solves

`readProxyErrorData` parses network error response bodies with `JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(bytes))` without try-catch. If a proxy returns non-JSON content in an error response body, the resulting SyntaxError escapes the caller's narrow error-pattern check (which only catches errors starting with "Proxy error body") and propagates as a confusing SyntaxError instead of falling back to the generic status-code error message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Same pattern as #109721 and #109754: JSON data from external network sources should be guarded with try-catch to prevent SyntaxError escape and enable graceful degradation.

## Evidence

- Existing proxy tests: 26/26 passed (2 test files)
- The fix wraps `JSON.parse` in try-catch, returning `undefined` on parse failure, which causes the caller at proxy.ts:332 to fall back to the generic `Proxy error: {status} {statusText}` message

## Merge Risk

Low. The caller already handles `undefined` return from this function, using the generic error message as fallback.

target.title: fix(github-copilot): prevent stale encrypted reasoning failures
target.body:
fix #95441

Related: #95493
Related: #95587

AI-assisted: yes (GitHub Copilot).

## What Problem This Solves

Persisted GitHub Copilot reasoning can become invalid when OpenClaw reconstructs a session, causing `invalid_encrypted_content` or a missing reply on a later turn. The rejection can happen while creating a Responses request or after its SSE stream opens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix uses the existing owner boundaries:

- **Cold replay history:** the GitHub Copilot provider's `sanitizeReplayHistory` hook removes persisted thinking/reasoning when a Copilot Responses `AgentSession` is rehydrated. The sanitized history becomes that session's in-memory state, while reasoning generated later in the same agent/tool loop remains available.
- **Active wire payload:** the provider boundary preserves complete native `rs_*` reasoning, converts Copilot connection-bound reasoning IDs to idless replay, keeps already-idless reasoning, and removes foreign, malformed, or incomplete reasoning. Existing message/function-call ID normalization remains intact.
- **Single bounded recovery:** Responses request creation and SSE draining share one retry budget. Before any public model output, a recognized encrypted-content failure retries once after removing only the top-level `encrypted_content` field from reasoning items. The retry preserves reasoning summaries and IDs, assistant messages, function calls, function outputs, and their order. Requests containing compaction fail closed instead of dropping compaction or constructing an item without its required ciphertext.

This separates prevention from recovery because neither is sufficient alone. Applying only a broad replay policy would discard valid same-loop continuity; relying only on recovery would keep sending known-stale state and make provider failure part of the normal path. Provider-owned cold sanitation plus one bounded generic fallback avoids both without adding session state, configuration, or a compatibility path.

The change adds no configuration, persisted replay state, transcript mutation, or public SDK surface.

## User Impact

Rehydrated Copilot sessions no longer send persisted opaque reasoning. Valid same-loop reasoning and tool continuation remain available. If a provider rejects stale reasoning before output starts, recovery preserves the continuation structure; compaction remains untouched and fails closed.

## Upstream Behavior References

- [`@github/copilot@1.0.69-2`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@github/copilot/v/1.0.69-2), build `546d22a58d`: active history retains encrypted reasoning, while cold resume, abort/cancel, and effective-model history rewrite strip opaque reasoning.
- [`github/copilot-sdk@5adb51b`](https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/5adb51b9e2ac50ad4876e756fa8c05549c1490fd/nodejs/src/generated/session-events.ts#L1044-L1054) documents OpenAI encrypted reasoning as session-bound and stripped on resume.
- [`microsoft/vscode@47657de`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L145-L172) requests `reasoning.encrypted_content`; its [history selection](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L306-L395) excludes pre-marker history, and its [serializer](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L631-L660) replays only complete Responses reasoning.
- OpenAI Node `6.45.0` models reasoning ciphertext as optional while compaction ciphertext is required; the recovery path therefore strips only reasoning ciphertext and never mutates compaction.
- #72602 records the live Copilot CAPI matrix: exact original or omitted reasoning IDs are accepted with original ciphertext; synthetic reasoning IDs are rejected.

## Evidence

- Current exact head: `243967371b74bc66113637dbc7ef099e45acaf69`; 8 files, `+729/-241` (970 changed lines, `size: L`).
- Builder-driven Responses continuation proof passed 57 tests, including create-time and streamed rejection, response-ID reset, one shared retry budget, abort/output-start guards, preservation of reasoning/message/function-call/function-output order, unchanged ID-only reasoning, and create/drain compaction no-retry.
- GitHub Copilot connection-bound-ID and stream-wrapper proof passed 15 tests. The focused cold-resume provider integration passed (1 test; 30 unrelated tests skipped).
- Targeted Oxfmt and Oxlint passed for all 8 PR files; `git diff --check` passed.
- Full local tsgo/aggregate lint was blocked by this linked worktree's stale dependency install missing existing `@types/web-push`; no dependency files are changed. Exact-head GitHub CI is running for the current commit.
- The primary cold-resume behavior was previously credentialed-live-tested on the unchanged provider sanitation path: one visible reply, `invalid_encrypted_content = 0`, and `LLM request failed = 0`. The current retry-only follow-up has no local Copilot credential, so that reactive fallback remains an explicit live-proof gap.
- Current-main manual review found no remaining actionable issue after replacing the destructive retry. The prior P1 path that removed reasoning/compaction while retaining tool continuation no longer exists.
- The test-only size compression retained all 57 focused cases; a read-only review found no weakened assertion or shared-state regression.

target.title: fix(gateway): config hot-reload permanently disables after sporadic recovered watcher errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running a long-lived gateway would silently lose config hot-reload: after a handful of transient file-watcher errors spread over the process lifetime, edits to `openclaw.json` stop being picked up until the gateway is restarted, even though every watcher recovery in between succeeded and served reloads normally.

The watcher re-create retry budget (3 attempts native, then degrade to polling, then 3 attempts polling, then `hot-reload disabled`) is consumed cumulatively across the whole process lifetime. A gateway that hits one recoverable inotify/kqueue error every few days — each followed by days of healthy watching — still marches irreversibly toward polling degradation and then permanent disable, because nothing ever refills the budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Watcher events (`add`/`change`/`unlink`) now route through a small wrapper that resets the re-create retry counter before scheduling the shared refresh path. A delivered file event is proof the recovered watcher works, so the bounded budget applies per failure episode instead of per process lifetime. Consecutive errors with no event in between still consume the same bounded budget, so genuinely persistent failures (e.g. exhausted inotify watches) degrade and disable exactly as before.

The reset intentionally hangs off the watcher event path only: `notifyPluginMetadataChanged` (added on current `main`) also calls the shared `scheduleExternalRefresh`, and a plugin-metadata refresh proves nothing about watcher health, so it does not touch the budget. The branch is rebased onto current `main` with that newer lifecycle behavior preserved.

## User Impact

Config hot-reload on long-lived gateways now survives sporadic recoverable watcher errors indefinitely. Persistent watcher failures behave exactly as before: bounded native retries, polling fallback, then a logged `config hot-reload disabled` with `hotReloadStatus()` reporting `disabled`.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof (real chokidar watcher, real file, real timers)

Driver: the production `startGatewayConfigReloader` watching a real temp `openclaw.json` with a real chokidar FSWatcher in native (non-polling) mode and real backoff timers. Each round performs a real `fs.writeFile` config edit (delivered by the real watcher and consumed by the reloader), then injects one transient error on the live FSWatcher instance — the same `error`-event path a kernel-level failure takes. Four rounds, one more than the retry budget.

Before (current `main`): the budget never refills, so recovered episodes still march toward degradation — the attempt counter climbs every round and round 4 exhausts native mode:

```
[proof] real watcher delivered a file event (#1)
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #1)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 1/3 in 500ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #1
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #2)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 2/3 in 2000ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #2
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #3)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 3/3 in 5000ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #3
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #4)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher native retries exhausted; degrading to polling mode: Error: simulated transient watcher failure #4
```

Four more sporadic-but-recovered errors in polling mode reach `config hot-reload disabled` permanently.

After (this patch): every recovered episode refills the budget — each error is `attempt 1/3`, the watcher stays in native mode, and hot reload stays active:

```
[proof] real watcher delivered a file event (#1)
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #1)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 1/3 in 500ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #1
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #2)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 1/3 in 500ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #2
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #3)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 1/3 in 500ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #3
[proof] config file edit consumed by reloader (commit #4)
[gateway-log][warn] config watcher error; re-creating watcher (attempt 1/3 in 500ms): Error: simulated transient watcher failure #4
[proof] round 4: hotReloadStatus=active watchersCreated=5
[proof] FINAL hotReloadStatus=active after 4 recovered errors
[proof] file events delivered=4, reload commits=4
```

### Regression coverage

- New test in `src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts` (`keeps hot-reload active when transient errors are separated by working watchers`): four error/recovery rounds, each recovered watcher proving itself with a delivered file event before the next error. Fails against unfixed `main` (fourth error degrades to polling despite every recovery working); passes with the fix.
- The pre-existing exhaustion tests (back-to-back errors with no event in between: degrade to polling, then disable) pass unchanged, proving persistent-failure behavior is preserved.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts` → 134 passed on the rebased head.
- Scoped `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` pass on the two changed files.

`parseSlugListJson` in the promotions-feed module parses JSON from the `notified_slugs_json` database column without a try-catch. target.title: feat(discord): show subagent progress
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord users can see a parent turn as idle while tracked subagents are still running. The source message provides no compact indication of concurrent child work or terminal failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core now emits one generic typed `subagent_progress` presentation event with source-message provenance. The Discord plugin maps that portable event to typing plus one count reaction, and retains a red reaction after a non-OK child outcome. One opt-in switch, `channels.discord.subagentProgress`, controls the behavior; emoji, cadence, and the one-hour typing bound remain internal defaults.

The maintainer rewrite deliberately keeps transport policy in Discord, routes native and tracked ACP spawns through the same core lifecycle, and persists only Discord reaction ownership and terminal outcome in plugin SQLite. Durable rows make count cleanup and failure presentation retry-safe across response loss and gateway restart without blocking subagent lifecycle delivery.

## User Impact

When enabled, the Discord source message shows `1️⃣` through `🔟` as tracked child concurrency changes, removes the count after the final child ends, keeps typing active for up to one hour, and leaves `🔴` for error, timeout, or killed outcomes. Other channels ignore the generic event and keep current behavior.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/subagent-progress.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.persistence.test.ts` — 69 passed across two shards.
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check` — baseline current.

- Contributor live Discord proof already recorded on this PR covered count add/replace/remove, concurrent children, channel/thread sources, typing drain, and a retained failure reaction. The rewrite preserves that user-visible shape while replacing the original configurable/internal hook design with the approved generic event and one-toggle contract.

target.title: fix(msteams): bound federated certificate file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createFederatedApp` (in `extensions/msteams/src/sdk.ts`) read the federated certificate path with an unbounded `fs.readFileSync(creds.certificatePath, "utf-8")`, so a misconfigured or oversized certificate file could trigger an unbounded read at credential-load time.

PR #109260 ran a credential-reader sweep that adopted `tryReadSecretFileSync` (with a `maxBytes` bound) across anthropic-vertex, google, gh-read, and mantis readers, but the MS Teams federated certificate read was missed. This applies the same helper there with a 1 MiB bound, so an oversized certificate file is rejected at the size check instead of being read whole. Missing or empty files still surface as the existing "Failed to read certificate file" error.

## Evidence

- The fix replaces `fs.readFileSync` with `tryReadSecretFileSync(..., ``maxBytes: 1_048_576, rejectHardlinks: false`)`, mirroring the #109260 sweep shape (e.g. anthropic-vertex/region.ts).
- `tryReadSecretFileSync` returns `undefined` for missing or over-limit files (its {BT}statSync().size > maxBytes{BT} guard), so the load path now throws "Failed to read certificate file ... file is empty or missing" in that case instead of proceeding with an empty/oversized key.
- Local vitest run of `extensions/msteams/src/sdk.test.ts` is green: 19 passed (19).
- New regression test mocks the helper returning `undefined` (the over-limit path) and asserts the load fails and `tryReadSecretFileSync` is called with the bound.

```ts
privateKey = tryReadSecretFileSync(creds.certificatePath, "MS Teams federated certificate", {
  maxBytes: MSTEAMS_CERTIFICATE_MAX_BYTES,
  rejectHardlinks: false,
}) ?? "";
```

```

      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

Sibling of #109260 (same tryReadSecretFileSync helper, same maxBytes-bound sweep); applies it to the MS Teams federated certificate read that the original sweep missed.

target.title: fix: keep session thinking through transcript recovery
target.body:
Closes #109275

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with stored `/think` or `/verbose` session preferences could lose those preferences when command-session resolution rotates the OpenClaw session id for terminal transcript-registry recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps stored thinking and verbose preferences available when terminal transcript recovery creates a replacement session id but the configured daily/idle reset policy would otherwise still treat the session as current. It intentionally does not carry those preferences when terminal recovery overlaps a configured daily or idle reset boundary, so a configured clean-session reset still wins.

target.title: fix(sqlite): add 10s SIGKILL timeout to mount lookup during WAL safety check
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readMountEntries()` in `sqlite-wal.ts` invokes `childProcess.execFileSync("mount", [])` without a timeout. On systems with unresponsive NFS/SMB mounts, the `mount` command can hang indefinitely, blocking the SQLite WAL safety check during startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing try-catch guards against execution failures, but cannot guard against a hung process. Adding `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` ensures the lookup is bounded (10s) and the process is forcibly terminated on timeout, matching the repository pattern used in `src/cli/ports.ts`, `src/tui/tui.ts`, and `src/daemon/program-args.ts`.

## Evidence

35/37 sqlite-wal tests pass (2 pre-existing failures due to SQLite version in test environment):

```
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  2 failed | 35 passed (37)
```

The change is a pure safety improvement — the existing catch block returns `[]` on failure, and the new options only add a time bound to an otherwise unbounded synchronous call.

## Merge Risk

Low — single-file change, nothing added to the public API surface. The function already has an empty-array fallback in its catch block, so the timeout path degrades gracefully.

target.title: fix: stabilize three tooling flakes at root cause (batch 3), incl. live-updater lock race
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Flake batch 3 under the no-rerun policy: three tooling flakes observed blocking landings on runs 29568640449 and 29569279237, each root-caused with a forced deterministic repro — one of them a real production bug in the live-updater's lock acquisition.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **check-extension-package-tsc-boundary "force-kills aborted async node step process groups"** — two mechanisms: (1) the #109140 class — `waitForFile` existence polls can catch `writeFileSync`'s open-truncate 0-byte window, parse NaN, and report a live process dead; replaced with `waitForPidFile` (poll until content parses to a positive pid) across all three sibling pid-read sites. (2) A teardown race: the fail-fast step exited on a 150ms fuse racing the aliveness assertion; now event-driven via an `abort.ack` file written strictly after the assertion. A 300ms injected stall reproduced the exact CI failure pre-fix and passes post-fix.
- **telegram-user-crabbox-proof "stops Crabbox recording when the desktop probe fails"** — the fake recorder published its pid file before installing its SIGTERM handler, while `recordProbeVideo` SIGTERMs the instant the probe throws; a recorder preempted in that window died to the default disposition and never wrote `recorder.term`. Handler now arms before the pid publish; same ordering applied to the three sibling fakes; the gateway-grandchild pid read is parse-validated inside its poll (a NaN pid silently skipped both the dead-check and the finally SIGKILL — leaked process). A 100ms forced spin reproduced the exact waitFor timeout deterministically pre-fix, passes post-fix.
- **`.agents/skills/openclaw-live-updater/scripts/update-main.mjs` — prod bug**: `acquireMaintenanceLock` gave only ENOENT the bounded creation-window retry; a reader hitting the racing writer's 0-byte window read empty `owner.json`, JSON.parse threw, and the script escalated to `invalid_lock` instead of a normal in-progress overlap. Any owner read/parse failure now re-reads within the same bounded 20x10ms budget; genuinely corrupt locks still throw `invalid_lock` after the budget. New frozen-window regression test failed with the exact CI error pre-fix, passes post-fix.

## User Impact

The live-updater fix is a real behavior fix: a maintenance-lock race no longer aborts updates with `invalid_lock` when it merely overlapped lock creation. The rest is test-only stability.

## Evidence

- Forced-interleaving repros flip fail→pass for all three (exact CI signatures).
- Stress: 10x per file at OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=6 — 30/30 green; full files green (22/30/53 tests; 105 after rebase re-run).
- Autoreview (codex gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): clean, 0 findings, "patch is correct (0.96)".

target.title: fix(config-cli,secrets): typed ExitError, JSON error output, and consistent stateDir for audit .env
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

### config get --json

`openclaw config get <path> --json` produces empty stdout when the config path does not exist. It only writes a text error message to stderr and exits with code 1. Automated consumers (scripts, CI) that pipe stdout expecting JSON receive nothing, making error handling unreliable.

### Secrets audit & apply .env path

The secrets audit and apply operations resolve the state directory for auth/model stores but re-resolve it for `.env`. If directory availability changes between calls (canonical `.openclaw` vs legacy `.clawdbot` directory appearing or disappearing), one operation can inspect or mutate two different state roots for the same run.

In `apply.ts` specifically, `projectPlanState` resolves `stateDir` once and uses it for config targets, auth stores, and legacy auth stores — but `scrubEnvFiles` calls `resolveStateDir` independently, so a root switch mid-operation can scrub a different `.env` and leave the intended plaintext credential untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

### config get --json

The `--json` flag implies machine-readable output on stdout. When a path is not found, the command now emits a structured JSON error on stdout, consistent with how `runConfigValidate` and `handleConfigMutationError` handle JSON-mode errors. The exit signal detection was also migrated from a fragile `__exit__:` string prefix match to the repository's typed `ExitError` contract.

### Secrets audit .env path

Reuse the already-resolved `stateDir` variable for constructing the `.env` path in `audit.ts`.

### Secrets apply .env path

Pass the `stateDir` already resolved by `projectPlanState` (line 296) into `scrubEnvFiles` instead of letting `scrubEnvFiles` call `resolveStateDir` again. This ensures auth stores (auth-profiles.json, auth.json) and `.env` are handled under the same state root for the entire apply operation.

## User Impact

- `openclaw config get nonexistent.path --json` now outputs `{"error": "Config path not found: nonexistent.path"}` to stdout (exit code 1)
- Non-JSON mode behavior is unchanged: error goes to stderr as before
- Secrets audit consistently reads `.env` from the same state directory as auth and model stores
- Secrets apply scrubs `.env` under the same state root as auth stores — no root-switch gap

## Evidence

### Real CLI proof — config get --json

**stdout:**
```
{
  "error": "Config path not found: nonexistent.path"
}
```
**stderr:** (build bootstrap logs only, no config command error output)
```
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs config get nonexistent.path --json
[openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale: dirty_watched_tree - dirty watched source tree).
...
```
**Exit code:** 1

### Real CLI proof — secrets audit

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR pnpm openclaw secrets audit --json
{
  "version": 1,
  "status": "findings",
  "filesScanned": [
    "/tmp/.../openclaw/.env",
    "/tmp/.../openclaw/openclaw.json"
  ],
  "summary": { "plaintextCount": 2, ... },
  "findings": [
    { "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND", "file": ".../openclaw.json", ... },
    { "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND", "file": ".../openclaw/.env", "jsonPath": "$env.OPENAI_API_KEY", ... }
  ]
}
```
Exit code: 0

### Real CLI proof — secrets apply (root-switch)

**Setup:** HOME contains both `.openclaw` (canonical) and `.clawdbot` (legacy) directories. Both have `.env` files with plaintext keys, plus `openclaw.json` with a plaintext `apiKey`.

**Before apply:**
```
-- .openclaw/.env (canonical, SHOULD be scrubbed) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-prod-plaintext-should-be-scrubbed
UNRELATED=keep-me

-- .clawdbot/.env (legacy, must NOT be touched) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-legacy-should-NOT-be-touched
UNRELATED=legacy-value

-- openclaw.json --
"apiKey": "sk-prod-plaintext-should-be-scrubbed"
```

**Command:**
```
$ HOME=$TMPHOME pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from plan.json
Secrets applied. Updated 2 file(s).
```

**After apply:**
```
-- .openclaw/.env (verify scrubbed) --
UNRELATED=keep-me

-- .clawdbot/.env (verify UNTOUCHED) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-legacy-should-NOT-be-touched
UNRELATED=legacy-value

-- openclaw.json --
"apiKey": {
  "source": "env",
  "provider": "default",
  "id": "OPENAI_API_KEY"
}
```

**Verification:**
- ✅ `.openclaw/.env` was scrubbed (plaintext key removed)
- ✅ `.openclaw/.env` preserved `UNRELATED=keep-me`
- ✅ `.clawdbot/.env` was NOT touched (legacy key still present)
- ✅ `.clawdbot/.env` preserved `UNRELATED=legacy-value`
- ✅ `openclaw.json` plaintext `apiKey` replaced with `SecretRef`

The plan targets `models.providers.openai.apiKey` with `scrubEnv: true`. `resolveStateDir` returns `.openclaw` when both directories exist, and the apply operation uses that single resolved `stateDir` for both auth stores and `.env` scrubbing. The legacy `.clawdbot/.env` is never touched.

### Tests

- `pnpm test src/secrets/apply.test.ts` — **31/31 passed** (includes new root-switch regression: "uses the same resolved stateDir for .env scrubbing as for auth stores")
- `pnpm test src/secrets/audit.test.ts` — **26/26 passed**
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — **130/130 passed**
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts` — **5/5 passed**

### Lint & Format

- oxlint: clean (`src/secrets/apply.ts`, `src/secrets/apply.test.ts`)
- oxfmt: clean

### New regression test — apply root-switch

The test sets up a HOME where both `.openclaw` and `.clawdbot` exist. `resolveStateDir` returns `.openclaw` when both exist (it checks `.openclaw` first). The test:

1. Writes a `.env` with a plaintext secret in `.openclaw` (canonical)
2. Writes a different `.env` with a dummy secret in `.clawdbot` (legacy)
3. Runs `secrets apply` with `scrubEnv: true`
4. Asserts `.openclaw/.env` was scrubbed (secret removed)
5. Asserts `.clawdbot/.env` was NOT touched (secret still present)

This proves one apply operation cannot switch roots mid-operation.

### Review findings addressed (revise round)

- **[P2] Reuse the operation's resolved state directory in apply** — `src/secrets/apply.ts:734`: `scrubEnvFiles` now accepts `stateDir` parameter and uses it instead of calling `resolveStateDir` again. Call site at line 341 passes the `stateDir` resolved on line 296.
- **[P1] Add root-switch regression** — `src/secrets/apply.test.ts`: New test "uses the same resolved stateDir for .env scrubbing as for auth stores" proves the invariant.

### Behavior addressed

- CLI JSON errors now reliably reach stdout consumers
- Exit signal contract migrated from `__exit__:` string sentinel to typed `ExitError`
- Audit `.env` lookup uses resolved `stateDir` instead of re-resolving
- Apply `.env` scrubbing uses the same `stateDir` as auth stores — single-root invariant

### What was not tested

- macOS-specific `realpath` symlink behavior (Linux CI parity)

target.title: fix(agents): emit diagnostic when sessions_yield parks without continuation evidence
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_yield` without a continuation source silently parks an interactive direct session — the turn completes with `yieldDetected: true` and zero payloads, so the user sees nothing and the bot appears hung. This adds a diagnostic payload when the yielded turn has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, async tools, or cron adds, so the user gets a visible message instead of a silent hang.

- **Problem**: `run.ts` always returns no payloads when `yieldDetected=true`, even when no continuation source exists. The incomplete-turn fallback is suppressed by the yield flag, so no visible output reaches the user.
- **Solution**: Extract a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` helper in `incomplete-turn.ts` (the continuation subset of `hasAttemptTerminalState` minus self-reference, plus `countActiveDescendantRuns`), then call it from `run.ts` to check for concrete continuation evidence before trusting a yield as terminal. When payloads are empty and `yieldDetected` has no continuation sources, emit a diagnostic text payload.
- **What changed**:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts` — new exported `hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt, activeDescendantCount?)` + `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant, placed next to sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` — inline predicate replaced with shared helper call; triple-nested ternary uses shared constant
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — 4 new tests: 3 diagnostic-suppression (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) + 1 async-tool purity
- **What did NOT change**: Yield acceptance semantics, `hasAttemptTerminalState`, `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`, liveness state classification. No existing yield path is altered.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #100065
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a model calls `sessions_yield` before establishing any continuation (before spawning subagents, sending messages, starting async tools, or scheduling cron work), the runtime accepts the yield unconditionally. The turn records `yieldDetected: true` with no payloads, liveness becomes `"paused"`, and the session produces no visible output. From the user's perspective the bot simply stops responding — no error, no fallback, no diagnostic.

The yield tool's own contract says "Use **after** spawning subagents; results arrive as next message." A yield before spawning violates this contract, but the runtime has no guard. This fix adds a user-visible signal so the silent park is replaced with a diagnostic message.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: `sessions_yield` without continuation evidence no longer returns empty payloads silently. A diagnostic text is emitted.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19, fix/yield-no-continuation-diagnostic-100065 branch
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Live proof: shared hasYieldContinuationEvidence logic (7 scenarios)
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { hasYieldContinuationEvidence } from "./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts";

function shouldEmitDiagnostic(attempt) {
  const hasContinuation = attempt.yieldDetected && hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt);
  if (attempt.yieldDetected && !hasContinuation)
    return { diagnostic: true, text: "⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume." };
  return { diagnostic: false };
}

const cases = [
  ["bare yield, no continuation", { yieldDetected: true }],
  ["yield + accepted spawn", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [{ runId: "c", childSessionKey: "k" }] }],
  ["yield + committed delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["answer"] }],
  ["yield + whitespace delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["   "] }],
  ["yield + empty spawn array", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [] }],
  ["yield + async tool in flight", { yieldDetected: true, toolMetas: [{ asyncStarted: true }] }],
  ["yield + approval prompt", { yieldDetected: true, didSendDeterministicApprovalPrompt: true }],
];
for (const [name, att] of cases)
  console.log(`${shouldEmitDiagnostic(att).diagnostic ? "DIAGNOSTIC" : "SILENT    "} — ${name}`);
NODE

# 2. Regression test suite (121 tests)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
# Real gateway run: sessions_yield without continuation → diagnostic emitted
$ openclaw agent --agent main --json --message 'Call sessions_yield. Do NOT spawn subagents, do NOT send messages, do NOT do anything else. Only call sessions_yield.'

{
  "result": {
    "payloads": [
      {
        "text": "⚠ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume.",
        "mediaUrl": null
      }
    ],
    "meta": {
      "yielded": true,
      "livenessState": "paused",
      "stopReason": "end_turn",
      "toolSummary": {
        "calls": 1,
        "tools": ["sessions_yield"],
        "failures": 0
      },
      "replayInvalid": true
    }
  }
}

# 7 production logic scenarios (node --import tsx)
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
DIAGNOSTIC — bare yield, no continuation
SILENT     — yield + accepted spawn
SILENT     — yield + committed delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + whitespace delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + empty spawn array
SILENT     — yield + async tool in flight
SILENT     — yield + approval prompt

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  121 passed (121)
```

```console
# Active descendant check: countActiveDescendantRuns() smoke test
$ node --import tsx -e "import { countActiveDescendantRuns } from './src/agents/subagent-registry-read.ts'; console.log('empty key:', countActiveDescendantRuns(''), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('unknown key:', countActiveDescendantRuns('no-such'), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('All returned 0 without throwing ✅');"
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. All 121 yield/incomplete-turn tests pass — no regression. Four new tests cover: (a) bare yield with no continuation → diagnostic emitted, (b) whitespace-only delivery text → NOT counted as continuation, (c) empty spawn array → NOT counted as continuation, (d) three suppression scenarios (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) → diagnostic suppressed.
  2. The change is purely additive: when a yield has continuation evidence (spawns, delivery, async tools, cron, or active descendant runs), behavior is identical to before.
  3. When a yield has no continuation evidence, a diagnostic payload `"⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume."` is emitted instead of an empty payload array.
  4. Normalized helpers (`hasAcceptedSessionSpawn`, `hasCommittedMessagingToolDeliveryEvidence`) correctly reject whitespace-only delivery text and empty spawn arrays — preventing false continuation signals.
  5. `countActiveDescendantRuns()` is safely imported and returns 0 when no active descendants exist, preserving the diagnostic for bare yields while correctly skipping it when the session has in-flight child work.

- **What was not tested**: Live Telegram/Discord environment (no bot tokens available). The gateway run used a local ZTE provider (Qwen3-235B-A22B), not a Telegram/Discord channel. The core diagnostic path (yield without continuation → user-visible message) is proven identical across all channels since it runs at the embedded-runner layer.

## Root Cause

Three compounding gaps allow the silent park:

1. **`sessions-yield-tool.ts`** — No validation at the tool level. Accepts any yield regardless of continuation state.
2. **`incomplete-turn.ts:261`** — `yieldDetected` causes `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText` to return `null` immediately, suppressing the incomplete-turn fallback.
3. **`run.ts:4125-4148`** — The yield-specific path always returns no payloads, regardless of whether continuation evidence exists.

This PR addresses (3) only — it is the safest additive fix. A deeper fix for (1) would require a product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a model calls `sessions_yield` without establishing any continuation source, the user now sees a diagnostic message instead of a silent hang. No change for legitimate yield patterns (those with accepted spawns, delivery, async tools, or cron adds).

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive change
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No. The new test file (`sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`) is additive — it does not modify existing serialized state or snapshots, requires no migration or upgrade path.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes, for the current scope. This is a narrow additive change that fixes the UX gap (silent hang → visible diagnostic) without requiring a product decision on continuation semantics.
- **Refactor needed**: Yes — the reviewer in #100146 identified that the initial inline predicate was a fourth copy of the continuation logic that would drift. The fix extracts a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` in `incomplete-turn.ts`, reuses `hasAsyncStartedToolActivity`, and places the `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant next to its sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`. `run.ts` is now orchestration-only for this path.
- **Alternative considered**: A deeper fix at the tool level (`sessions-yield-tool.ts`) that rejects yields without continuation evidence. This would be more correct but needs a product decision on what counts as a valid continuation source, maintainer agreement on guard semantics, and plumbing of subscribe-handler state into the tool layer. Marked as future work.

### Future work (Step 2)

A follow-up PR could validate continuation sources inside `sessions_yield` tool execution and reject a yield that has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, or async work. This requires:
- Access to subscribe-handler state from the tool layer
- A product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source
- Tests for the rejection path

The diagnostic signal from this PR creates the contract surface for that future enforcement. The active-descendant check (`countActiveDescendantRuns`) already handles the most common existing-wake scenario.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None. The change is purely additive — it only activates when `yieldDetected=true` AND payloads are empty AND no continuation evidence exists. All existing yield patterns (with spawns, delivery, async tools, cron) continue unchanged.
- **Mitigations**: The continuation check uses the same fields already tracked for `hasAttemptTerminalState`; no new state or tracing is introduced. Suppression tests (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) guard against always-false regression in the shared helper.
- **Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. Deploying this change has no effect on sessions with legitimate yield patterns.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

---

target.title: fix(ui): blend chat pane header with window chrome and stroke workspace chip icons
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat pane header renders an accent-tinted "peel" whenever the pane is active. With a single pane that is always, so the title-bar strip sits on a red-tinted band (pink in light mode) that clashes with the neutral window chrome next to it — most visibly in the macOS app where this header is the top window surface beside the traffic lights, but the same seam shows on the web next to the sidebar.

The workspace chip's folder icon (and the cloud globe for cloud-worker sessions) also rendered as solid black shapes: the Lucide outline icons in this header never received the `fill: none; stroke: currentColor` treatment, so the paths fell back to browser-default black fill — a dark blob on both themes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The active-header wash (`.chat-pane__header--active`, 8% `--accent`) is redundant: a lone pane needs no focus marker, and split view already outlines the focused pane with the `.chat-split-view__cell--active` accent ring. Deleting the wash (rather than retinting it) leaves one canonical focus indicator and lets the header blend with the surrounding chrome in every theme. The now-unused `active` prop was removed from `ChatPaneHeaderProps` and its caller.
- The chip/cloud icon rule gains the same Lucide stroke treatment `.btn svg` uses (`fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.5px`, round caps/joins), with a comment explaining why it must stay.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(anthropic): add claude-fable-5 to CLI allowlist, aliases, labels, and context window
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`claude-fable-5` — a production Anthropic model — was missing from the CLI provider path (`extensions/anthropic/cli-constants.ts` + `cli-catalog.ts` + `openclaw.plugin.json`), while the direct Anthropic provider path (`register.runtime.ts`) already has full support via `isAnthropicFable5Model()` / `resolveAnthropicFixedContextWindow()`.

Five metadata layers were missing, plus the `fable`/`fable-5` aliases weren't routed through the context/model-ref canonicalization paths:

| Layer | File | Consequence |
|-------|------|-------------|
| allowlist | `cli-constants.ts` | `openclaw configure` cannot select fable-5 |
| aliases | `cli-constants.ts` | `fable` / `fable-5` aliases unresolvable |
| static manifest | `openclaw.plugin.json` | `openclaw models list` hides fable-5 |
| label | `cli-catalog.ts` | Falls back to bare `${id} (Claude CLI)` |
| context window | `cli-catalog.ts` | Falls back to 200K instead of 1M |
| context/model-ref canonicalization | `claude-model-refs.ts`, `prepare.ts` | Bare `fable` alias uses 200K fallback instead of 1M |
| **fixed context window resolver** | `context-resolution.ts` | `claude-cli` excluded from Fable 5/Mythos 5 provider checks |

This is the same root cause as #100572: a new model was registered in the direct API path but the CLI path's independently-maintained constants were not updated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add fable-5 entries to all CLI metadata layers **and** route the `fable` family alias through both canonicalization paths:

1. `cli-constants.ts`: add `claude-cli/claude-fable-5` to allowlist, add `fable`/`fable-5`/`claude-fable-5` aliases
2. `cli-catalog.ts`: add 1M context window, friendly label, and large-image tier for fable-5
3. `openclaw.plugin.json`: add `claude-fable-5` to the static `claude-cli` provider manifest so `openclaw models list --all` shows the model
4. `claude-model-refs.ts`: add `fable: "claude-fable-5"` to `DEFAULT_CLAUDE_MODEL_BY_FAMILY` so `resolveClaudeCliAnthropicModelRefs("claude-cli/fable")` returns the correct 1M reference
5. `prepare.ts`: add `fable`/`fable-5` aliases to `CLAUDE_CLI_CONTEXT_MODEL_ALIASES` so context budgeting doesn't fall to the 200K default
6. `context-resolution.ts`: add `claude-cli` to the Fable 5 and Mythos 5 fixed context window provider checks
7. `cli-migration.test.ts`: update 3 migration test expectations to include `sonnet-5`/`fable-5` entries produced by the updated allowlist, plus a regression test covering `fable`/`fable-5`/`claude-fable-5` canonicalization in both bare and provider-qualified forms

## User Impact

- `openclaw configure` can now select `claude-fable-5` for the Claude CLI provider
- `openclaw models list --all --provider claude-cli` now shows `claude-cli/claude-fable-5` with correct 1M context
- Aliases `fable` / `fable-5` / `claude-fable-5` resolve with correct 1M context window (was 200K)

## Evidence

### Tests

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts extensions/anthropic/index.test.ts` — 60 passed (includes new fable alias canonicalization regression test)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/context.test.ts` — 80 passed (includes `claude-cli/claude-fable-5` and `claude-cli/claude-mythos-5` context-window cases)

#### 1. CLI Model Catalog (end-to-end)

#### 3. Config Defaults Pipeline (configure model-picker path)

```

```

#### 5. Alias Canonicalization (bare + provider-qualified, exact head)

Direct execution of `resolveClaudeCliAnthropicModelRefs` from `extensions/anthropic/claude-model-refs.ts` at this head:

```
fable                        => rewriteRef=anthropic/claude-fable-5

claude-fable-5               => rewriteRef=anthropic/claude-fable-5

Current `main` rewrote Anthropic fixed-context handling since the first reviewed head. After rebasing, this PR's remaining diff in `src/agents/context-resolution.ts` is exactly the intended two-line change — adding `provider === "claude-cli"` to the existing Fable 5 and Mythos 5 provider checks; all of main's newer provider-capability logic and current Mythos handling are preserved (verified via `git diff upstream/main..HEAD` and the 80 passing `context.test.ts` cases, which cover main's rewritten resolution paths).

A review finding proposed mapping `fable-5` to the family name `fable` instead of `claude-fable-5`. Runtime verification against the actual canonicalizer contract shows the current mapping is correct and the proposed change would break it:

target.title: fix(discord): cancel response body on webhook error path
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

`throwWebhookResponseError()` reads the error body with `readResponseTextLimited` (8 KiB cap) and throws a `RateLimitError` or `DiscordError`. The caller uses `proxyFetch ?? fetch` — neither provides a guarded-fetch release mechanism. When the error body exceeds the cap, unconsumed bytes keep the TCP connection open until GC.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `void response.body?.cancel()?.catch(() => {})` after reading the error body, before the branching throw. One line covers both the 429 rate-limit path and the generic error path. Follows the `cancelUnreadResponseBody` pattern.

## User Impact

Discord webhook error responses now release TCP connections promptly. Successful webhook deliveries are unaffected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.proxy.test.ts --run`: **12/12 passed**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `throwWebhookResponseError` has two throw sites (429 and generic); the cancel is placed before the branching so both paths benefit.

```
BEFORE: readResponseTextLimited(response, 8192) → reader cancelled at limit
        → throw RateLimitError/DiscordError → TCP may stay open

AFTER:  readResponseTextLimited(response, 8192) → reader cancelled at limit

target.title: fix(clickclack): cancel response body on HTTP error path
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

`createClickClackClient.request()` uses raw `fetch` (no guarded-fetch release mechanism). On non-ok responses it reads the error body with `readResponseTextLimited` (8 KiB cap) and throws `ClickClackHttpError`. When the error body exceeds the cap, `readResponseTextPrefix` cancels the **reader** but the underlying `response.body` stream may retain unconsumed bytes, keeping the TCP connection open until GC.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `void response.body?.cancel()?.catch(() => {})` after reading the error body, before throwing. This explicitly signals the fetch implementation to abort the TCP connection for unconsumed bytes. Follows the same pattern as `cancelUnreadResponseBody` in lmstudio and `response.body?.cancel()` in anthropic/clawrouter/venice.

## User Impact

ClickClack API error responses now release TCP connections promptly instead of waiting for GC. Successful responses are unaffected.

target.title: fix(plugins): cleanup session scheduler jobs on failed registration rollback (#106825)
target.body:
Closes #106825

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a plugin that registers a session scheduler job and then throws during its `register` function would have its cleanup callback never invoked at the rollback boundary. The live session-scheduler record remained in module-global runtime state while the registry metadata was correctly restored — leaving external plugin-owned scheduler work (via `cleanup`) uncancelled after a failed registration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registration rollback (`createPluginRegistrationTransaction`) restores the registry snapshot and calls `rollbackPluginGlobalSideEffects` to clean up commands, interactive handlers, code-mode namespaces, context engines, and hooks — but did not clean up session scheduler jobs. These jobs are stored in two layers: a `registry.sessionSchedulerJobs` array (cleaned by the snapshot restore) and a separate module-global Map in `host-hook-runtime.ts` (previously never cleaned on rollback).

The fix adds the existing `cleanupPluginSessionSchedulerJobs` call to the `rollbackPluginGlobalSideEffects` function in `registry.ts`, filtered to the rolling-back plugin's records. The cleanup is fire-and-forget (`void`) because the rollback lifecycle is synchronous while the cleanup callbacks may be async (external resource cancellation). Any cleanup failures are logged as warnings via `pushDiagnostic`.

## User Impact

Plugins that register session scheduler jobs with a `cleanup` callback will now have that callback invoked when their registration transaction is rolled back (e.g., a later exception during the same `register` function). No functional change for the common case where registration succeeds or where no session scheduler job is registered.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(sms): prevent silent loss of acknowledged Twilio messages
target.body:
Related: #109657

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where incoming Twilio SMS/RCS webhooks could receive a successful TwiML response before OpenClaw had durably admitted the message. Dispatch then ran as detached in-memory work behind a 10-minute/10,000-entry replay guard, so a process failure after the HTTP 200 could silently lose an inbound message; after a 200, Twilio has no failed request to retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SMS plugin now writes the signature-validated raw Twilio form to the shared SQLite channel-ingress queue before returning 200. The durable event id uses Twilio's `MessageSid`, `SmsSid`, or `SmsMessageSid` aliases, sender identity selects the serialized lane, and startup plus interval pumps recover queued work after restart. Parsing and account validation happen at dispatch and permanent invalid payloads are dead-lettered.

The old in-memory replay guard and its saturation 429 path are removed. Completed tombstones retain 24 hours/20,000 entries, strictly covering the retired 10-minute/10,000-key window.

The earlier autoreview P1 claiming ambiguous non-adopted settlement was rejected after tracing the core lifecycle seam: `bindIngressLifecycleToReplyOptions` carries adoption, deferral, and abandonment into reply admission; deferred or abandoned work settles through those callbacks, while a normal non-adopted return is terminal local handling. This matches the Telegram reference adapter's `skipped -> completed` mapping.

## User Impact

Acknowledged inbound SMS/RCS messages survive OpenClaw restarts and drain in sender order without replaying completed `MessageSid` events. If durable admission fails, OpenClaw does not acknowledge the webhook. Existing Twilio SID aliases remain accepted.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/sms` — 12 files, 85 tests passed. Coverage includes restart recovery, original receipt timestamps, completed tombstones, handler-reload guard parity, enqueue-before-ack failure, permanent invalid-payload/account dead-lettering, canonical sender lanes, and all Twilio message SID aliases.
- `oxfmt --check <touched SMS files>` — clean.
- `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json <touched SMS files>` — clean.
- `node scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mjs` — production/full-tree/script scans: 0 unused exports.
- `node scripts/check-deadcode-unused-files.mjs` — production/full-tree scans: 0 unused files.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — clean.
- Fresh whole-branch autoreview after the SID-alias, sender-lane, and receipt-timestamp fixes — no accepted/actionable findings.
- Twilio documents `SmsSid` and `SmsMessageSid` as deprecated aliases with the same value as `MessageSid`, and documents connection retry policy separately: https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/guides/webhook-request and https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/webhooks/webhooks-connection-overrides

Proof gap: no live Twilio-number round trip was run; this worktree has no live number/public callback target. The signed HTTP webhook, durable SQLite restart, replay, and failure paths are covered by the focused tests above.

target.title: feat(gateway): add ticketed read-only MCP App host
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I understand the implementation and completed fresh autoreview passes with no accepted/actionable findings. No agent transcript is included because separate approval was not provided.

Closes #109851

## Summary

- Add a generic standalone MCP App host that exchanges a short-lived signed view ticket instead of exposing the operator Gateway bearer token.
- Keep the trusted shell on the Gateway origin and reuse the separate static sandbox listener; no view secret or dynamic app data enters the listener document.
- Keep the standalone host deliberately read-only and add one official `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` fixture that drives both the existing authenticated Control UI host and the new standalone host over the real browser/transport path.

## What Problem This Solves

Future channel and standalone browser launches need to render one MCP App view without handing the page a reusable operator credential. The existing authenticated Control UI host is not a least-privilege launch boundary for an external browser surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

A process-local HMAC capability is bound to the current OpenClaw session key, MCP runtime session, view id, and view-lease deadline. The new HTTP boundary reconstructs only that live view, while the static host implements the stable MCP Apps initialization, ping, input/result, sizing, and teardown messages and rejects tool/resource requests.

This reuses the existing MCP runtime, view lease, sandbox proxy, and Gateway configuration. It adds no config/env surface, protocol version, channel launch UX, approval flow, or privileged capability.

## User Impact

When MCP Apps are already enabled, an authenticated Gateway client can obtain a standalone URL for the current view and open it without exposing the Gateway bearer token. Existing Control UI behavior is unchanged. There is no new default UI or channel action in this PR.

## Independent Landing and Backward Safety

- Existing `mcp.app.view` fields and semantics are preserved. `standaloneUrl` and its expiry are optional additions; ticket capacity, expiry races, or unexpected issuance failures omit those fields while returning the original successful view payload.
- The two new HTTP paths exist only behind the existing `mcp.apps.enabled` gate. Disabled installations and all other routes retain current behavior.
- The standalone URL is fully functional on this PR alone: initialize, ping, input/result delivery, read-only denials, reload, teardown, and rejection states require no later MCP Apps PR.
- The existing Control UI keeps its current app-only tool/resource authority. The conformance fixture proves shared/app-only tools and app resources remain available there while model-only tools remain denied.
- No current UI consumes the optional standalone field, and no current capability advertisement changes.

Exact dormant/additive boundary: the new route and optional Gateway response field are additive behind the existing MCP Apps gate. No launch button, channel integration, approval UI, tool/resource capability, or later-PR contract is advertised. A later PR may expose the already-working URL in channel UX, but is not required for any behavior enabled here.

## Evidence

- Real transport/browser path: an official self-contained `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps@1.7.4` app ran through a real stdio MCP server, Gateway WebSocket authentication, Control UI Vite host, Gateway HTTP routes, static sandbox listener, and nested postMessage transports.
- Both hosts completed the stable `2026-01-26` initialize handshake and standard MCP `ping`, then received the original tool input and result.
- Control UI baseline: server tool/resource capabilities were advertised; the app-only companion tool and app resource succeeded; a model-only tool was denied.
- Standalone boundary: neither server tools nor server resources were advertised; tool and resource calls were denied; the only authorization header was `MCP-App v1...`, never `Bearer test`.
- Lifecycle: app-requested teardown removed the frame, reload reconstructed it, and a second load received the original result.
- Ticket security: unit/integration coverage rejects tampered, expired, wrong-session, wrong-runtime, wrong-view, replaced-view, and inappropriate reuse states; the browser scenario proves tampered and expired URLs fail.
- Origin/CSP review: the shell is static on the Gateway origin, the iframe is restricted to the exact separate sandbox origin, the listener stays static, the ticket remains in the URL fragment and is sent only in the dedicated authorization header, responses are no-store/no-referrer, and the shell never receives the Gateway token.
- Two final full-branch autoreviews after simplification/fixes reported no actionable findings. A reviewer-found missing standard `ping` response was fixed and exercised in both host modes before the clean final pass.

## Verification

- `pnpm build` — full runtime and Control UI production build passed, including plugin SDK export and Control UI performance gates.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed with the frozen lockfile.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-app-standalone.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts ui/src/e2e/mcp-app-conformance.e2e.test.ts` — 13 gateway assertions and the complete Chromium conformance scenario passed.
- `git diff --check` and targeted `oxfmt` — passed.
- Repeated canonical-base updates were rebased without conflicts; every final `git range-diff` showed all three commits patch-identical. The push used a fresh `upstream/main` fetch and verified ancestry immediately before publication.
- Blacksmith Testbox passed the build and broad static gates before exposing two strict fixture type errors that were fixed. Two later Testbox leases failed during delegated file sync before executing code, so trusted-source exact-head fallback proof ran in isolated temporary clones with frozen dependencies.

## Simplification and Scope

The PR is six files: three production files plus two focused Gateway tests and one maintained browser fixture. Net production growth is 463 LOC. Most of that is the single standalone module owning the capability store, HTTP/security boundary, static shell, and minimal protocol bridge; keeping those concerns together avoids a new public abstraction or duplicated policy. The remaining production additions are narrow route and optional-response wiring. No cleanup, config, launch UI, or privileged capability is mixed in.

## Known Gaps

- This does not add channel launch UX, approval UI, or standalone tool/resource authority.
- Tickets are intentionally process-local and expire no later than the view lease; a Gateway restart invalidates them.
- At the bounded live-ticket capacity, existing view responses continue to work but omit a standalone URL until capacity expires.
- Required GitHub CI on the published head remains the final landing gate.

target.title: feat(slack): support running as a real Slack user (user identity)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Today OpenClaw's Slack channel can only run as a Slack **app/bot** — it appears as an app in the member list, is `@mention`-gated, and fundamentally cannot participate in the places people actually talk: a bot can never join a 1:1 DM or an existing group DM. Operators who want an agent that behaves like a real teammate (posts under a human's name, gets DMed, replies in group DMs) have no supported way to do it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an opt-in, account-level `identity: "bot" | "user"` mode for the Slack plugin (default `"bot"`, so existing setups are unchanged).

`identity: "user"` authenticates as the authorizing human via a **user OAuth token (`xoxp`)** for all reads and writes, so messages appear under that person's name. A minimal **companion app** carries realtime events subscribed **"on behalf of users"** (Events API, Socket Mode or HTTP) — which is the *only* official mechanism to receive DMs and group DMs, since delivery is scoped to what the authorizing human can see and no bot can be present in those conversations.

We deliberately rejected the browser-session-token (`xoxc`/`xoxd`) "self-bot" approach used by chat bridges: it is unofficial, ToS-grey, session-fragile, and Slack is sunsetting the last legacy realtime path (classic apps end 2026-11-16). The user-token + companion-app path is the officially supported route.

Design notes: one identity-aware `resolveSlackOperationToken` (the duplicated `userTokenReadOnly` gate was removed); the human's own `user_id` (from `auth.test` on the user token) becomes the mention/DM target and the self-send dedupe source, so the agent never replies to its own messages; `@slack/bolt` runs token-less via `token: userToken` (verified against Bolt source). No `xoxc`/`xoxd`, no bot user required.

## User Impact

- Operators can opt a Slack account into acting as a **real person** (`identity: "user"`), including full DM and group-DM participation, with the companion app as invisible plumbing.
- **Existing bot setups are unaffected** — `identity` defaults to `"bot"` and all bot-identity behavior is byte-neutral; no config migration.
- Docs add the exact companion-app recipe (user scopes, on-behalf-of-user event subscriptions, Socket/HTTP config examples) in `docs/channels/slack.md`.

## Evidence

- **Full Slack plugin suite green**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack` → 121 files / 1922 tests passing, confirmed stable across 5 consecutive parallel runs (a shared-state test flake surfaced during review and was fixed — see the final commit).
- **Typecheck**: `tsgo:core` / `tsgo:extensions` / `tsgo:extensions:test` clean (Blacksmith Testbox).
- **Review**: each slice independently reviewed (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`); the transport's token-less Bolt startup and self-send dedupe were verified directly against `@slack/bolt` source; the token model against Slack's official docs.
- **Behavior-neutral for `identity: "bot"`**: no existing bot-identity assertions changed.

**Known validation gap (intentional, opt-in):** live delivery of bot-less user-scope `message.im`/`message.mpim` events is documented by Slack via the scope/visibility model but is thinly exercised in the wild; end-to-end verification in a live workspace is pending. Because the feature is opt-in and default-`bot`, this does not affect existing users — the live check is a fast-follow, and any Slack-side wrinkle is a documented follow-up rather than a regression.

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707

## What Problem This Solves

`applySkillProposal` in the Skill Workshop wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation. Plan or change-description proposals could silently overwrite real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. This is the canonical apply-boundary fix for #107707; the merged generation-side hardening (PR #108339) explicitly left apply-side validation unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The initial patch used heading-presence and any-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that (1) heading checks block valid headingless skills, (2) any-line overlap is trivially bypassable — a plan document sharing a single heading or boilerplate line receives `requiresExplicitApproval=false` and overwrites the skill, and (3) zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

The current fix validates proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser, rejects empty bodies, and uses a **substantial-continuity classifier** that requires at least 3 shared non-heading body lines AND at least 50% of original non-heading content retained before allowing automatic apply. Low-continuity updates force pending approval even under `auto` policy, preserving an explicit replacement path for intentional complete rewrites while blocking incidental-overlap plans that share only headings or 1-2 boilerplate lines.

## User Impact

- Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected with a descriptive error; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Proposals without valid SKILL.md frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Low-continuity update proposals (insufficient shared content with current SKILL.md) are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy, instead of being silently auto-applied
- Substantially continuous updates (≥3 shared non-heading lines, ≥50% original content retained) apply normally without requiring explicit approval
- Valid headingless skill updates apply normally when they retain substantial content
- Valid updates with shared content display a bounded change summary (`+N lines, -M lines`) in approval descriptions and apply results
- Rollback data (`previousContent`) is recorded in `rollback.json` for all successful applies

**Maintainer decision needed**: The low-continuity approval override changes the recently established automatic approval policy (PR #107690). This conditional exception requires explicit maintainer confirmation from shakkernerd (who introduced the automatic approval behavior). Options: (1) Keep the safety exception — require explicit approval only for low-continuity updates while substantially continuous updates continue using automatic approval (recommended). (2) Preserve unconditional automatic approval — reject structurally invalid proposals but allow all structurally valid updates to retain automatic approval. (3) Require approval for every update — simpler safety rule but more workflow regression.

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, **exact head SHA `b50fd7ca78`**

**Approval-hook proof: auto policy blocks low-continuity writes while allowing high-continuity updates**

The `resolveSkillWorkshopToolApproval` function is the approval hook that determines whether an agent-initiated `apply` action proceeds automatically or requires operator approval. Under `auto` policy, it returns `undefined` (no approval required) for actions that pass all checks. For low-continuity updates, it returns `requireApproval` with a warning prompt, which blocks the agent from applying the proposal until the operator approves. SKILL.md remains unchanged until approval is granted.

```

    title: "Apply workspace skill proposal"
    severity: "warning"
    timeoutMs: 70000
    allowedDecisions: ["allow-once", "deny"]
  → Agent cannot auto-apply; SKILL.md stays unchanged until operator approves

High-continuity update (4 of 6 shared non-heading lines, 67% retained):
  resolveSkillWorkshopToolApproval returns undefined
  → Agent can auto-apply; normal workflow continues
```

**Incidental-overlap regression proof (exact head SHA `b50fd7ca78`)**:

The substantial-continuity classifier blocks all three incidental-overlap variants that previously bypassed approval:

```

Heading-only overlap (shares "# Weather" heading, no non-heading overlap):

  → requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅

1-line overlap (shares "Steps to check weather.", 1/3=33%):
  overlapCount=1, ratio=0.33 → 1<3 && 0.33<0.5 → isSubstantialContinuity=false
  → requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅

2-line overlap (shares "Steps to check weather." + "Check the forecast.", 2/3=67%):
  overlapCount=2, ratio=0.67 → 2<3 → isSubstantialContinuity=false
  → requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅

Substantial continuity (shares 4/6 non-heading lines, 67%):
  overlapCount=4, ratio=0.67 → 4≥3 && 0.67≥0.5 → isSubstantialContinuity=true
  → requiresExplicitApproval=false, auto-apply proceeds ✅
```

@
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` could buffer an unbounded response body via `response.text()` when fetching the Discord `/gateway/bot` metadata endpoint.

## Rebase Note

Rebased onto current main (9ddd988c9) to pick up the rename `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` → `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout`. The private helper `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` is now re-exported for direct testing.

## What Changed (vs previous revision)

- **Rebased onto main**: Resolved merge conflicts with the `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` rename and added test for stalled DNS preflight.
- **Re-exported `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo`**: The function was un-exported during the main rename; re-exported so bounded-read tests can target it directly.
- **Fixed lint**: Added curly braces to `if (res.destroyed) return;` one-liners in the test (eslint `curly`).

## Why This Change Was Made

**Streaming pre-read bound (primary path):** When the response body stream is available, the function now uses `readResponseWithLimit` to enforce the 4 MiB cap **before** buffering — the stream is read in chunks and cancelled on overflow, matching the existing `materializeGuardedResponse` pattern used by `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded`.

**Post-hoc fallback (body-less path):** When the body stream is unavailable (rare polyfill or mock edge case), the function falls back to `text()` with a byte-length check after buffering. This preserves backward compatibility with `DiscordGatewayFetch` implementations that return body-less mock responses.

**Non-transient overflow:** Size overflow now throws as non-transient (`transient: false`) so the detail message propagates to callers instead of being swallowed by the generic "fetch failed" wrapper.

target.title: refactor: move MCP OAuth state to SQLite
target.body:
Closes #109842

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where native MCP OAuth credentials and authorization state used a separate JSON-plus-file-lock store. That storage model sat outside OpenClaw's canonical state database and made refresh, logout, migration, and cross-process conflict handling depend on filesystem behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

MCP OAuth now uses the shared SQLite state database as its only runtime store. Login, refresh, logout, resource challenges, and terminal token rejection run under a shared SQLite lease; the HTTP transport keeps authorization retries inside that fenced owner. `openclaw doctor --fix` is the sole legacy migration owner: it imports exact validated JSON under exclusive state ownership, records a receipt, verifies cleanup, and never creates a runtime fallback.

The migration intentionally does not dual-read or dual-write. Malformed, ambiguous, changing, or contended legacy state remains in place with actionable Doctor output. A replacement token rejected by the resource is marked for explicit reauthorization, preventing refresh loops across later requests.

AI-assisted implementation. I reviewed the storage, migration, OAuth, MCP SDK, and Codex projection paths and understand the resulting ownership model.

## User Impact

New MCP OAuth sessions persist only in `state/openclaw.sqlite`. Existing installations with files under `state/mcp-oauth` must run `openclaw doctor --fix`; valid credentials are imported and the retired JSON is removed only after verification. Corrupt or actively owned files fail closed.

Operators gain serialized cross-process refresh and logout behavior, request cancellation during OAuth work, preserved challenge metadata, and a clear explicit-login path when refreshed credentials are rejected.

Release note: MCP OAuth credentials and refresh state now persist in SQLite. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` once to import legacy MCP OAuth JSON.

## Evidence

- 86 focused state-lease, OAuth resolver, bearer retry, transport, and Doctor migration tests pass across four Vitest shards.
- Blacksmith Testbox changed gate passed formatting, generated baselines, core and test typechecks, full core lint, Kysely/database-first guards, SDK boundaries, import cycles, and architecture checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29567071520
- Final structured autoreview: clean, no accepted or actionable findings.
- Independent exact-tree audit: pass; verified abort cleanup, challenge precedence, orphan-expiry rejection, terminal refresh-loop prevention, and stale-token fencing.
- Source-blind CLI smoke emitted only the normal shared SQLite bootstrap state and no retired OAuth JSON, JSONL, TXT, or lock sidecar.
- MCP SDK 1.29.0 source was checked for authorization, discovery, and transport retry behavior.
- Codex source at `35b33e4304a262965d3816da36d4991802fd5269` was checked for MCP bearer projection and refresh behavior; Codex continues to receive the same bearer-only configuration and no refresh token.
