target.title: fix(skills): filter NaN from Date.parse in history scan session cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resumePendingForBatchScan` in `src/skills/workshop/history-scan.ts` built session cursors by calling `Date.parse(session.updatedAt)` without filtering out `NaN`. When a session's `updatedAt` is missing, malformed, or otherwise not parseable, `updatedAtMs` became `NaN`, which then propagated through the resume cursor into subsequent scan iterations.

The downstream comparison `cursor.updatedAtMs > lastReviewedAtMs` returns `false` when `updatedAtMs` is `NaN`, so affected sessions were silently skipped on resume instead of being re-scanned from the correct point.

## Fix

Filter `sessionCursors` so any entry whose `updatedAtMs` is not a finite number is dropped before it can reach the resume cursor. This preserves existing behavior for valid timestamps while ensuring malformed ones cannot poison the resume state.

Export `toStoredState` as a named export (instead of wrapping it in `__testing`) so the knip production deadcode scan does not flag it as unused.

target.title: fix(sqlite): stop mount probes blocking database startup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite startup falls back to the system `mount` command when `/proc/self/mountinfo` is unavailable. That synchronous probe had no deadline, so a stalled `mount` process could block state or plugin database initialization indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback probe now has a one-second hard timeout. If filesystem classification times out, SQLite conservatively uses rollback journaling instead of assuming WAL is safe. Existing behavior for successful mount classification and non-timeout probe failures is preserved.

## User Impact

Database-backed OpenClaw startup no longer waits indefinitely on a wedged mount probe. When the deadline is reached, startup continues with rollback journaling, avoiding both the hang and an unsafe WAL assumption for an unclassified network filesystem.

## Evidence

- Regression-first tests cover the missing timeout and the conservative timeout policy.
- Before: the production `configureSqliteWalMaintenance` path with an isolated stalled `mount` fixture exceeded a 4-second external guard (`exit_status=124`).
- After: the same production path returned in about 1.0 seconds, selected `journal_mode=delete`, and exited successfully.

target.title: fix(plugins): handle NaN from Date.parse in catalog rollback detection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two catalog rollback guards compared timestamps returned by `Date.parse` without checking for `NaN`:

1. `isHostedCatalogSignedFeedRollback` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.ts`
2. `isMonotonicRollback` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-snapshot-store.ts`

Both used `Date.parse(candidate.generatedAt) < Date.parse(current.generatedAt)`. When either `generatedAt` string is missing, malformed, or otherwise not parseable, `Date.parse` returns `NaN`, and `NaN < NaN` evaluates to `false`. The rollback guards therefore reported "not a rollback" and accepted a candidate that should have been rejected, allowing the catalog snapshot store to move backward to an older or malformed snapshot.

## Fix

Mirror the same defensive policy in both guards:
- If the **candidate's** `generatedAt` is invalid (`NaN`), conservatively treat it as a rollback so malformed candidates cannot downgrade the store.
- If the **current** snapshot's `generatedAt` is invalid, treat the candidate as newer (not a rollback) so a broken current state can still be repaired.

Export `isHostedCatalogSignedFeedRollback` and `isMonotonicRollback` as named exports (instead of wrapping in `__testing`) so the knip production deadcode scan does not flag them as unused. Both functions are already called from production code.

## Evidence

- **Local test run** (10 regression tests pass):
  ```
  RUN  v4.1.9
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  10 passed | 35 skipped (45)
  ```
- **New tests cover**: candidate invalid → rollback; current invalid → not a rollback; equal-sequence timestamp comparison; newer/older by sequence.

target.title: fix(browser): preserve config source in headless mode fallback
target.body:
Closes #109673

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who set `browser.headless: true` in `openclaw.json` would see `browser status` report `headless: false (default)` and `browser start` launch Chrome with a visible window, ignoring the documented config key. The only workaround was passing the explicit `--headless` CLI flag on every start.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `resolveManagedBrowserHeadlessMode` function's final fallback path hardcoded `source: "default"` even when `resolved.headlessSource` was `"config"`. This meant the config-derived headless value was returned correctly (`resolved.headless`), but the source was always reported as `"default"`, causing status display to show `headless: false (default)` and preventing the headless flag from being applied during Chrome launch in certain code paths.

The fix uses `resolved.headlessSource ?? "default"` instead, preserving the actual source through the entire precedence chain. Three regression tests cover the previously untested scenario of `browser.headless: true` on non-Linux platforms with the default openclaw profile.

## User Impact

Operators who set `browser.headless: true` in their config will now see `browser status` correctly report `headless: true (config)` and `browser start` will launch Chrome with `--headless=new --disable-gpu` as documented, without requiring the `--headless` CLI flag.

## Evidence

- All 86 existing browser config tests pass
- All 53 Chrome internal tests pass
- 3 new regression tests added:
  - `honors global browser.headless=true for the default openclaw profile on non-Linux` — proves `resolveManagedBrowserHeadlessMode` returns `{ headless: true, source: "config" }` when `browser.headless: true`
  - `reports headless=false with source=default when global config is unset on non-Linux` — proves the default case still works
  - `preserves config source in the final fallback when resolved.headlessSource is config` — directly exercises the fixed fallback path by constructing a profile with `headlessSource: "default"` while `resolved.headlessSource` is `"config"`

target.title: feat(ui): complete Control UI MCP App bridge
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I understand the implementation and completed fresh autoreview passes with no accepted/actionable findings. No agent transcript is included because separate approval was not provided.

## Summary

- Complete the existing Control UI MCP App host bridge with safe, text-only `ui/message` support routed through the normal visible chat-send path.
- Advertise messaging only for fresh, authorized app views; reconstructed views remain explicitly read-only.
- Propagate live theme and iframe dimensions through the official MCP Apps host-context bridge without remounting, with observer/listener cleanup on teardown.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI could render MCP App resources and service app tool/resource requests, but an app could not safely ask the user to send plain text through the host chat, and mounted apps did not receive live theme or size changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the already-present iframe/resource reconstruction architecture. It reuses the existing widget-prompt validation and `WIDGET_PROMPT_EVENT` send seam, adds host-owned exact-text confirmation for MCP App requests, and uses the official `AppBridge.setHostContext` lifecycle. It does not add a second send route, config/env surface, protocol version, or privileged approval path.

The implementation adds a small explicit `readOnly` lease marker because a fresh app may legitimately have zero app-callable tools, while a transcript-reconstructed preview must remain resource-only. Tool-count inference could not represent both states safely.

## User Impact

When MCP Apps are already enabled, a visible and focused fresh app can request that the user send one plain-text message. The host shows the exact text for confirmation, then sends through the existing chat composer path. Hidden/background frames, empty or oversized text, slash commands, and rate-limit excesses are rejected. Apps also receive current theme and dimensions as they change.

## Independent landing and backward safety

- The gateway response field is additive. Older Control UIs ignore it; a newer UI talking to an older gateway sees the field absent and installs/advertises no message handler.
- Existing widget prompts use the same extracted validation/send helper without the MCP App confirmation callback; their existing behavior is covered by the widget-prompt and tool-card regression suites.
- App tool/resource handlers, app-only policy, sandbox origins, inner opaque iframe isolation, routes, config, and protocol versions are unchanged.
- Fresh views with an explicit authority set may advertise messaging even when that set is empty. Legacy views without authority and reconstructed `readOnly` views fail closed.
- No behavior enabled by this PR requires a later MCP Apps PR.

Exact dormant/additive boundary: all behavior remains behind the existing `mcp.apps.enabled` gate. Within that gate, `message.text` is advertised only when a fresh view has explicit current-run authority and the host handler is installed. Reconstructed views can still render/read resources but cannot message or call tools. Rich or multi-block `ui/message` content is intentionally unsupported.

## Evidence

- Genuine browser flow: a browser-bundled `App` from `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` ran through the real Control UI Vite app, dedicated sandbox HTTP server, and nested iframe bridge. The official initialize handshake advertised `message.text`; exact host consent was required; accepted text produced the normal `chat.send` request (`deliver: false`); the app received its response; live light-theme and container-dimension changes propagated without remounting.
- Focused exact-head proof: 89/89 assertions passed across MCP view leases, transcript reconstruction, gateway authorization, text/focus/visibility/size/rate/slash boundaries, existing widget prompts, host-context updates, and cleanup.
- Production build passed, including the Control UI lazy chunk (`mcp-app-view-registration`, 63.26 kB) and Control UI performance limits.
- Changed-surface checks passed through formatting, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and related policy gates. An earlier Plugin SDK baseline mismatch was independently reproduced on untouched canonical main; the current canonical base includes its unrelated generated/declaration repairs.
- A first CI run exposed a production lint suppression for the SDK's request-style `onmessage` setter. The handler now registers through that documented public setter via a typed wrapper, without a suppression or private schema import; the component and suppression-ratchet tests pass, followed by two clean fresh autoreviews.
- Two fresh autoreviews after the final safety fixes reported no actionable findings (confidence 0.98 and 0.94). Canonical-base updates preserved the exact nine-file product diff.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.test.ts src/gateway/mcp-app-reconstruction.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-security.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.node.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.widget-prompts.test.ts`
- Exact-head `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm build`
- Fresh `$autoreview` passes before and after simplification/final safety edits

## Simplification and scope

The PR changes five production files and four focused test files. Net production growth is +60 LOC: the message handler/host-context lifecycle and explicit read-only authority marker are offset by deleting the duplicated widget-prompt policy/send implementation. No additional abstraction module, route, config, or compatibility shim was added.

## Known gaps

- This does not enable MCP Apps globally or implement later rollout work.
- Only one plain text content block is accepted; rich content remains rejected.
- Transcript-reconstructed previews intentionally remain read-only until a fresh run grants current authority.

target.title: fix(gateway): ignore invalid handshake timeout env for Gateway calls
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

`callGateway` treated any non-empty `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` value as an active handshake timeout override when choosing the default wrapper timeout. That included invalid values such as `"0"` or `"abc"`.

The shared preauth timeout resolver already rejects those values and falls back safely, but the Gateway call wrapper only checked whether the env var existed. That made the wrapper timeout policy diverge from the shared timeout contract: an invalid env value could incorrectly extend the default wrapper timeout from `10000ms` to the preauth default of `15000ms`.

### Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway call wrapper should only align its default timeout with a valid preauth handshake override. Invalid env values should behave like no env override, leaving the wrapper at its normal `10000ms` default unless a valid config timeout is present.

This change adds `getPreauthHandshakeTimeoutMsFromEnv()` next to the existing connect-challenge env helper and routes both `resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` and `callGateway` through that shared parser. The result is one canonical env contract:

| input                                      | shared preauth env value | call wrapper default |
|--------------------------------------------|--------------------------|----------------------|
| unset                                      | none                     | `10000ms`            |
| `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS="0"`        | invalid / ignored        | `10000ms`            |
| `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS="abc"`      | invalid / ignored        | `10000ms`            |
| `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS="30000"`    | `30000ms`                | `30000ms`            |
| `gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs: 30000` config | `30000ms`                | `30000ms`            |

### User Impact

Users and operators who accidentally set an invalid handshake timeout env value now get the normal Gateway call timeout behavior. Valid positive integer env overrides continue to extend the wrapper timeout as before for slower or loaded hosts.

### Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior addressed:** invalid `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` values were ignored by the shared resolver but still treated as an active wrapper timeout override by `callGateway`.
- **Real environment:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.13.1, commit `135aa7a002` on branch `fix/gateway-invalid-handshake-env-timeout`.
- **Exact proof before this patch:** a temporary regression test set `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS="0"`, called real `callGateway({ method: "health" })` with the silent test Gateway client, advanced fake timers by `10000ms`, and expected `gateway timeout after 10000ms`.
- **Observed result before fix:** the assertion failed because the error message was still empty after `10000ms`.
- **Exact current-behavior confirmation before this patch:** the same temporary test passed when asserting no timeout at `10000ms`, then advancing another `5000ms` and expecting `gateway timeout after 15000ms`.
- **Evidence after fix:** the committed regression test now sets `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS="0"` and verifies the wrapper times out at `10000ms`.
- **What was not tested:** a live Gateway process with a real invalid shell env; the focused test exercises the same `callGateway` timeout path with the real timeout resolver and fake timers.

### Tests and Validation

```
$ OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-client/src/timeouts.test.ts src/gateway/handshake-timeouts.test.ts src/gateway/call.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.gateway-client.config.ts
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 16.46s
```

```
$ git diff --check
EXIT=0
```

Formatting was applied with the existing local formatter binary:

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write packages/gateway-client/src/timeouts.ts packages/gateway-client/src/timeouts.test.ts src/gateway/handshake-timeouts.ts src/gateway/call.ts src/gateway/call.test.ts
Finished in 382ms on 5 files using 6 threads.
```

One package-level regression assertion added: invalid preauth handshake env values return `undefined` from the shared env helper.

One Gateway call regression assertion added: invalid `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS="0"` does not extend the default wrapper timeout past `10000ms`.

### Risk Checklist

- **User-visible behavior:** Yes, only for invalid env values. Invalid `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` no longer extends Gateway call wrapper timeout.
- **Config/env/migration behavior:** Env behavior is touched, but no new env var or config key is added. Valid env values keep existing behavior.
- **Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution:** No.
- **Plugins/providers/channels/SDK:** No plugin/provider behavior changed. The change is in the private Gateway client timeout helper and Gateway call wrapper.
- **Highest-risk area:** Gateway timeout behavior for callers relying on handshake timeout env/config alignment.
- **Mitigation:** Shared parser keeps env semantics consistent with existing preauth resolver tests; focused Gateway call regression covers the invalid env wrapper timeout path; existing valid env/config alignment tests continue to pass.

Closes: N/A

target.title: feat(feishu): bot-to-bot conversation support with @mention handling
target.body:
## Summary

Makes Feishu bot-to-bot conversations actually work. Bot-authored messages already reach dispatch on `main` (nothing gates them out), so bots could already "talk" — but the experience was broken: replies frequently never reached the peer bot because the `@mention` was missing or used the wrong syntax for the payload, so the conversation silently died. This PR makes bot-to-bot replies reliable — correct, payload-aware `@mention` delivery on every visible path (text, chunked, card, streaming) — and adds opt-in (`allowBots`) plus loop-protection controls. (In a Feishu group a message only notifies the entities it explicitly `@mentions`, so a reply without the right `@` is silently never delivered.)

- Continue treating incoming bot messages like user messages (now gated by an `allowBots` opt-in) so the agent can take part in bot-to-bot threads.
- New `bot-name` resolution module backed by the bot batch API as a weak dependency: falls back to the `open_id` when the bot info scope is absent.
- Per-chat mention registry resolving display name → `open_id` for outbound use.
- Outbound mention handling: teach `<at user_id="...">` syntax in the system prompt, strip only the leading self-mention, preserve + dedup other mentions, escape `<`/`>` in display names.
- Guarantee bot-to-bot replies `@mention` the bot sender via a deterministic `ensureMention` backstop, applied **per outbound unit** (every text chunk and the streaming-card close) using the **syntax that matches the payload** — `<at user_id="...">` for text/post messages, `<at id=...>` for lark_md cards — so the peer bot is notified on every visible path. Replies are delivered inline, not in a topic thread.
- `allowBots` opt-in (default: accept, preserving current behavior) lets operators set `false` to ignore bots or `"mentions"` to accept only when `@mentioned`.
- Shared bot-pair loop guard: bot-authored turns are wired into core `botLoopProtection` (sliding window, on by default) plus a Layer-1 self-filter that drops the bot's own webhook echoes.
- Core owns the group reply-delivery mode; the feishu `@mention` hint stays delivery-mode-agnostic (no duplicate delivery-mode computation in the plugin).

Aligns with #71396 — main no longer auto-prepends mentions, so this does not reintroduce the third-party mention cascade: the `mentionTargets` block stays context-only and never tells the model to re-`@` listed users.

Scope: changes are under `extensions/feishu/**` plus the feishu docs page. The one non-plugin file is `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts`, regenerated (`pnpm config:channels:gen`) because the new `allowBots`/`botLoopProtection` config fields must appear in the aggregated bundled-plugin config metadata that the config-metadata check validates.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/feishu` — green, including the new/updated `outbound-mention`, `reply-dispatcher`, `bot` (bot-authored handling), and `monitor` suites covering card vs text mention syntax, per-chunk mentions, `allowBots` gating, and loop-guard suppression.
- `pnpm config:channels:gen --check`, `tsgo`, and `oxlint` clean for the touched surface.
- Real-machine verification in a live Feishu group (see proof below).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a group bot-to-bot reply now `@mentions` the bot sender so the other bot actually receives it — across text messages, chunked replies, and lark_md cards; replies to a human still `@` the human; a silent turn stays `NO_REPLY`. With `allowBots: false` the bot ignores other bots' messages. Previously a bot replying to a bot could omit the `@` (or use the wrong card syntax) and the reply was silently never delivered.

Real environment tested: a live Feishu group containing two bots and one human participant; the agent ran as one bot and replied across multiple turns to the other bot and to the human, under both text and card render modes, and with `allowBots` toggled. (Identifiers below are redacted.)

Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran `pnpm config:channels:gen`, rebuilt and restarted the gateway, then drove a multi-turn bot-to-bot exchange in the live group; captured the agent session trajectory and compared it against the messages actually delivered to the group; toggled `allowBots` and a tight `botLoopProtection` window to observe gating.

Evidence after fix:

- On turns where the sender was the other bot, the inbound prompt carried `[System: "<name>" (open_id: ou_<bot-sender-redacted>) is a bot and receives your reply only if you @mention it. You MUST @mention it in your reply.]`, and the reply led with the bot sender's `<at>` — the peer bot received it.
- `ensureMention` backstop verified live: on a turn where the raw model output omitted the bot sender's `@`, the message actually delivered to the group still contained it — the dispatcher backfilled it.
- Card path verified live: a reply rendered as a lark_md card carried the card mention syntax (`<at id=...>`) and the peer bot received it (the text-form tag would not have notified inside a card).
- `allowBots` verified live: with `allowBots` disabled, the peer bot's messages no longer triggered a reply.

Copied live output from the session (open_ids and names redacted):

```text
# Inbound prompt to the agent — sender is the other bot:
[System: "<bot>" (open_id: ou_REDACTED) is a bot and receives your reply only if
 you @mention it. You MUST @mention it in your reply.]

# Agent reply that turn, as delivered to the group — leads with the bot sender's <at>:
<at user_id="ou_REDACTED"><bot></at> 好，背景比较清晰，… (reply continues)

# A later turn whose raw model output dropped the bot-sender @ (it only @'d the
# human). The message ACTUALLY delivered to the group still carried it — the
# dispatcher's ensureMention backfilled the bot sender before sending:
<at user_id="ou_REDACTED"><bot></at> <at user_id="ou_REDACTED_HUMAN"><human></at> 面试结论：…
```

Observed result after fix: the other bot received and continued the conversation across turns under both text and card modes; no silent drop. `allowBots: false` cleanly suppressed bot-authored replies. Replies addressed exactly the intended target and stayed inline.

What was not tested: the `message_tool` visible-reply path does not receive the deterministic backstop by design (see Design notes); that is an intentional product decision, not an untested gap.

## Design notes

- **Per-payload mention syntax.** Feishu uses two `<at>` forms: `<at user_id="...">Name</at>` for text/post messages and `<at id=...></at>` for lark_md cards. The backstop emits the form matching each outbound unit and re-applies it per chunk and on streaming-card close, so a long or card-rendered bot-to-bot reply notifies the peer on every message.
- **The deterministic backstop is intentionally scoped to the `automatic` reply path, not `message_tool`.** `automatic` is an implicit reply where the agent does not directly control delivery, so the dispatcher guarantees the bot-sender `@`. The `message_tool` path (`messages.groupChat.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`) is an explicit, flexible send where the agent deliberately authors the message, recipients, and mentions; the plugin respects what the agent wrote and does **not** auto-inject — forcing one would override an intentional, author-controlled send. Outbound mention normalization still runs on both paths, so any `@` the agent does write is resolved correctly.
- **Bot-pair loop protection.** Bot-authored messages already reached dispatch on `main` (no gate drops them), so the bot-pair possibility is not introduced here. This PR adds the safety: `allowBots` (default accept; `false`/`"mentions"` to restrict), a Layer-1 self-filter that drops the bot's own webhook echoes, and wiring of accepted bot-authored turns into core's shared `botLoopProtection` sliding-window guard (on by default). Tunable/disable-able via `channels.feishu.botLoopProtection`.

target.title: fix(doctor): repair ALTER-appended operator approval schema instead of wedging startup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a hard startup wedge where `openclaw gateway` refuses to start and `openclaw doctor --fix` circularly reports "has a legacy operator approval schema; run openclaw doctor --fix to migrate it" — leaving the user with no working path. Hit in production on a macOS install whose state database predates the `resolution_ref` column.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fail-closed matcher in `openclaw-state-db-operator-approval-migration.ts` only accepted the exact canonical-position legacy DDL. A real shipped upgrade path added `resolution_ref` via `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` (see `ensureAdditiveStateColumns`), producing a tail-appended nullable column. That shape failed the exact match, the repair no-oped, and `assertCanonicalStateSchemaShape` threw the same message doctor tells you to fix with doctor.

Three fixes, all fail-closed:
1. The matcher now accepts exactly four enumerated shapes: canonical-position or ALTER-appended `resolution_ref`, each STRICT or non-STRICT. Arbitrary schema differences still refuse migration.
2. The copy filters rows that cannot satisfy the canonical `resolution_ref TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(length = 43, charset)` constraint (pre-ref rows hold NULL; non-STRICT tables can even hold BLOBs). Approvals are transient runtime state, so nonconforming rows are dropped rather than aborting the repair and re-wedging startup.
3. The table rebuild now replays only the operator-approval index statements instead of the entire canonical schema — executing the full schema mid-repair fails on many-versions-behind databases whose other tables still lack columns the later additive/STRICT repairs add ("no such column: agent_id").

Also: when the repair itself refuses or fails inside doctor, the warning no longer recursively recommends `doctor --fix`.

target.title: improve: let Code Mode use declared tool result shapes
target.body:
Related: #109288
Follow-up to #109651 and #109290

AI-assisted: Yes (Codex)

## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode learned exact tool ids and compact input signatures from #109651, but every tool result still appeared as unknown. Even when a tool had a stable structured result, models often spent one exec returning the raw value and another exec processing fields they could have known up front. This left avoidable model turns, tokens, and latency in common multi-operation workflows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trusted OpenClaw core and plugin tools can now declare an optional `outputSchema` for `AgentToolResult.details`. Code Mode and Tool Search expose a bounded TypeScript-style output hint only when that schema is complete and closed; open, oversized, unsupported, MCP, and client schemas remain unknown and raw-first.

OpenClaw compiles trusted output schemas before execution, then validates final details after normal hooks. The compact renderer has strict depth/property/character/union bounds. Remote and client schemas stay deferred as `input: "unknown"` and use object identity for catalog reuse, preventing attacker-sized metadata walks while preserving schema-replacement invalidation. `agents_list` adopts the contract as the first built-in example.

The change also promotes Code Mode to a dedicated `/tools/code-mode` documentation page with Quickstart, runtime semantics, guest API, output-contract authoring, trust/validation rules, fallback behavior, debugging, and validation guidance. The old `/reference/code-mode` route redirects to it.

## User Impact

Code Mode can call and process tools with declared result shapes in the first exec instead of paying a raw-inspection round trip. Unknown outputs keep the safe existing raw-first behavior. Plugin authors get one documented result contract shared by Tool Search and Code Mode, without trusting remote MCP or client schema claims.

## Evidence

Live multi-provider matrix: four validated Code Mode tasks per provider over the real Agent runtime and a 72-tool catalog with adversarial decoys. Baseline is merged #109651; after is this branch.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

target.title: fix(acp): persist spawn label to target session store instead of requester store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `/acp spawn <agent> --label <name>` creates an ACP session for a **different agent** than the requester (e.g. from `main` into `claude` or `codex`), the operator-supplied `--label` was silently lost. Follow-up commands that resolve sessions by label — `/focus <label>`, `/acp status <label>`, and `sessions.resolve` — would fail with "No session found with label".

The root cause is a **store-partition mismatch** in `persistSpawnedSessionLabel`:

- The session key is `agent:claude:acp:<uuid>` (owned by the target agent, e.g. `claude`)
- But the label was persisted to the requester's store (`commandParams.storePath` → `agents/main/sessions/`)
- The requester's store has no entry for `agent:claude:acp:…`, so the write is a silent no-op
- The spawned session's store (`agents/claude/sessions/`) never receives the label

Session key generation always uses the target agent id (`spawn.agentId`), so this affects every cross-agent `/acp spawn` flow.

Fixes #106136

## Why This Change Was Made

`persistSpawnedSessionLabel` now resolves the canonical store path from the **spawned session key** via `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` (`src/acp/runtime/session-meta.ts:76`) instead of using the requester's `storePath`. The in-memory `sessionStore` is only mutated when both stores resolve to the same path (same-agent spawn).

`resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` was previously unexported and only used internally in `session-meta.ts`. This PR exports it so `lifecycle.ts` can reuse the same canonical store-resolution boundary already trusted by sibling ACP metadata operations (`upsertAcpSessionMeta`, `listAcpSessionEntries`, `readAcpSessionEntry`).

## User Impact

- **Before**: Cross-agent ACP spawn labels (`/acp spawn claude --label novel`) were silently dropped. `/focus novel` failed. Only full session keys (`/focus agent:claude:acp:<uuid>`) worked.
- **After**: Labels persist to the correct target store regardless of which agent issues the spawn. `/focus <label>` and `/acp status <label>` work as expected for cross-agent ACP sessions.
- Same-agent spawns are unaffected — the store path resolves to the same location and behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Unit tests**: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts` — **67/67 passed**
**Typecheck**: `pnpm check:test-types` — passed
**Build**: `pnpm build` — passed

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Cross-agent ACP spawn label persistence — label written to target agent's session store, resolved via `sessions.resolve` by label.

Real environment tested: Linux x86_64 (kernel 4.19.112-2.el8), Node v24.15.0, branch `fix/acp-spawn-label-106136`, binary `OpenClaw 2026.7.2`.

**Gateway** — started with acpx lazy backend, 12 plugins loaded:

```
$ OPENCLAW_SKIP_ACPX_RUNTIME_PROBE=1 node dist/index.js gateway --port 18789
http server listening (12 plugins: acpx, anthropic, browser, canvas, codex, device-pair,
  file-transfer, memory-core, memory-wiki, minimax, phone-control, talk-voice; 3.4s)
gateway ready
```

**Cross-agent spawn** — `/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795` via Gateway WebSocket `chat.send` RPC, requester `main_assistant`, target `claude` (acpx backend):

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"chat.send","params":{"sessionKey":"agent:main_assistant:main",
     "message":"/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795",...}}
<<< {"runId":"proof-spawn-...","status":"started"}

[event] chat reply:
  ✅ Spawned ACP session agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3
  (persistent, backend acpx).
```

**Label resolution** — `sessions.resolve` by label via Gateway WebSocket:

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"sessions.resolve","params":{"label":"proof-1784006976795"}}
<<< {"ok":true,"key":"agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3"}
```

**Session list confirmation** — cross-agent session appears in list with correct label:

```
agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3 → label="proof-1784006976795"

```

Observed result after fix:
- `/acp spawn claude --label` → session created as `agent:claude:acp:…` in target (claude) store ✓
- `sessions.resolve({label})` → returns `agent:claude:acp:…` (cross-agent owner) ✓

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Preserve result control through normal, deferred-directory, Tool Search, and Code Mode catalog execution paths.
- Reject unsupported finalized controls with an explicit tool error.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1, rebased on current main.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

target.title: fix(coding-agent): isolate Codex CLI CODEX_HOME from OpenClaw OAuth in skill launch forms
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users launching Codex workers from the bundled
`coding-agent` skill could reuse the ambient `~/.codex` ChatGPT OAuth state
that OpenClaw also depends on, which can leave one client failing with
`refresh_token_reused`.

Fixes #109704

## Why This Change Was Made

The manual Codex launch forms now require an authenticated `CODEX_HOME` outside
every Git worktree, and the scratch recipe logs in the isolated home before
running `codex exec`. The credential warning now matches Codex's supported
storage modes instead of implying that OAuth state is always in `auth.json`.

## User Impact

Users can run Codex background workers without placing Codex credentials in a
checkout or accidentally launching scratch workers from an empty auth store.

## Evidence

- Codex source inspection: `CODEX_HOME` selects the Codex home directory, and
  CLI auth may use file, keyring, or auto keyring-with-file-fallback storage
  (`codex-rs/utils/home-dir/src/lib.rs`, `codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs`,
  `codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs`, `codex-rs/login/src/server.rs`).
- Negative control: a fresh empty `CODEX_HOME` reports `Not logged in`, so the
  old scratch shape cannot complete an authenticated turn without login.
- Real scratch path: a temporary Git repo plus an authenticated external
  `CODEX_HOME` completed `codex exec` and returned the requested message.
- `pnpm docs:list`
- `git diff --check 5024c100a3244d605a7f874d3d48c842110f6a5c...HEAD`

```text
$ TMP_CODEX_HOME=$(mktemp -d); chmod 700 "$TMP_CODEX_HOME"; CODEX_HOME="$TMP_CODEX_HOME" codex login status
Not logged in

$ SCRATCH=$(mktemp -d); git -C "$SCRATCH" init
$ CODEX_HOME=<authenticated-external-home> codex login status
Logged in using ChatGPT
$ CODEX_HOME=<authenticated-external-home> codex exec --skip-git-repo-check -C <tmp-git-repo> --output-last-message <proof-output> 'Reply exactly: isolated-codex-home-ok'
workdir: <tmp-git-repo>
last_message:
isolated-codex-home-ok
```

target.title: fix(ai): preserve Unicode in provider error bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could receive malformed provider error text when an external API response body placed an emoji or another non-BMP character at the truncation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared provider-error formatter now uses the existing UTF-16-safe truncation helper instead of splitting the string at an arbitrary code unit. This keeps the existing 4,000-code-unit cap and output format unchanged while preventing lone surrogates.

## User Impact

Provider failures continue to include a bounded response-body excerpt, but the excerpt is now valid Unicode even when the boundary falls inside an emoji.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression case with 3,999 ASCII code units followed by an emoji, reproducing the exact split boundary.
- Node 24 Docker proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/utils/provider-error.test.ts` passed 1 file / 5 tests.
- `git diff --check` and targeted `oxfmt` passed.
- Fresh branch autoreview against current `upstream/main` completed with no actionable findings.

### Exact-head built-package boundary proof

- Inspected successful CI run `29564719443` for exact head `c38921555e5234e91ea6a07abd3861120abda0b7`; `build-artifacts` and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed.
- Downloaded `dist-runtime-build` artifact `8400705348`; archive SHA-256 is `9863a46e89b98e2a216a581128774d0f02d59e9719cf583eceb9561842ed0f2b`, and `zstd -t` passed.
- The artifact contains 44 emitted files under `packages/ai/dist`. Searching that entire tree for `@openclaw/normalization-core` returned zero matches.
- `provider-error-CDmoLcmM.mjs` imports `truncateUtf16Safe` through the relative chunk `./transform-messages-Dz5aG0D0.mjs`; that chunk contains the bundled `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts` implementation.

This proves the workspace helper is bundled into the emitted `@openclaw/ai` JavaScript and is not an unresolved runtime dependency.

### Packaged provider-adapter runtime proof

- Created an npm tarball from the exact-head CI `packages/ai/dist` output and the exact-head package metadata; tarball SHA-256 is `3f11d7f3db37e7992948547d03a062e300bc0bb1c6ec4a3bf11c1970581c6faa`.
- Installed that tarball with scripts disabled into an empty consumer. The installed dependency tree does not contain `@openclaw/normalization-core`.
- Under Node `v24.18.0`, imported the public `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai` entry and ran `streamSimpleOpenAICompletions` against a loopback OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint.
- The adapter sent `/v1/chat/completions`; the endpoint returned a 502 JSON error whose independently serialized long body placed the emoji's high surrogate at code-unit index 3,999.

Redacted output:

```text
PACKAGED_PROVIDER_PROOF_109786 {"packageEntry":"@openclaw/ai/internal/openai","requestPath":"/v1/chat/completions","serializedErrorBoundary":3999,"stopReason":"error","errorMessageLength":4019,"endsWithTruncationMarker":true,"hasLoneSurrogate":false,"boundarySuffix":"xxxxxxxx... [truncated]"}
```

This is an installed-package and real provider-adapter HTTP-path probe using a local deterministic error endpoint. It does not claim an external provider credential run.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance; the behavior, dependency boundary, diff, and test evidence were reviewed before submission.

target.title: feat(gateway): handle Feishu VC meeting invites
target.body: ## Summary - Register Feishu `vc.bot.meeting_invited_v1` in the bundled `feishu` monitor dispatcher. - Convert valid VC meeting invite events into synthetic inbound Feishu direct-message turns from the inviter, reusing the existing DM pairing, allowlist, dynamic agent creation, session recording, and reply-dispatch path. - Ask the agent to join immediately by meeting number, with instructions to pass `call_id` only when the installed join tool exposes that parameter. - Route follow-up replies to the real Feishu inviter target (`user:` / `user:`), not a synthetic meeting route, so the normal `message` tool and final replies stay on the supported Feishu DM channel. - Document the required `vc.bot.meeting_invited_v1` event subscription for meeting invite auto-join. ## Linked context Fixes #91677. Supersedes #89751 with the same final behavior on a clean single-commit branch. This PR is based on the Feishu VC meeting invite behavior tested from live bot invitations and the sibling Feishu invite flow. ## Real behavior proof Behavior addressed: Feishu VC bot meeting invite events now reach OpenClaw through the bundled `feishu` plugin and trigger an immediate meeting-join turn while preserving the normal Feishu reply/session route back to the inviter. Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw gateway using the linked bundled `extensions/feishu` plugin, with a live Feishu bot and live VC meeting invitations. Exact steps or command run after this patch: Built and installed the OpenClaw branch locally, verified the gateway was loading `openclaw` rather than the older external `openclaw-lark` plugin, restarted the gateway after rebuilding, sent live Feishu VC meeting invitations to the bot, inspected gateway/runtime logs and agent tool invocations, then reran the focused validation commands listed below. Evidence after fix: Runtime logs showed `feishu[default]: vc meeting invited, dispatching synthetic inbound` for live meeting invites. The join path invoked `lark-cli vc +meeting-join --meeting-number ... --format json`; one invalid meeting returned Feishu code `121005` (`meeting not exist`), and a later live invite joined successfully with a meeting number, meeting id, start time, and topic returned by Feishu. Focused tests assert the finalized inbound context uses `To` and `OriginatingTo` as the inviter's supported Feishu DM target, creates a Feishu reply dispatcher for that target, and does not call the removed direct acknowledgement send path for dispatched invites. Observed result after fix: The live Feishu invite event was accepted by the `feishu` plugin, converted into a synthetic inbound turn, joined the meeting by meeting number, and kept follow-up agent replies on the inviter's standard Feishu direct-message route instead of `vc-meeting:`. What was not tested: I did not attach screenshots or sanitized transcript artifacts to the PR. The live validation used local gateway logs and Feishu runtime/tool output rather than a published artifact. Proof limitations or environment constraints: The real-environment proof depends on a live Feishu bot, live meeting invite, and local gateway configuration. The PR therefore includes focused regression tests for the dispatch, dedupe, reply target, pairing-blocked, user_id-only pairing, and compatibility branches so the behavior remains reviewable without access to that live Feishu environment. ## Tests and validation - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/monitor.vc-meeting-invited-handler.test.ts` - `pnpm check:test-types` - `node scripts/run-bundled-extension-oxlint.mjs` - `git diff --check` - `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` - clean, no accepted/actionable findings ## Risk checklist - User-visible behavior: yes. A Feishu VC invite to the bot can now create an inbound turn that attempts to join the meeting. - Configuration/operator action: yes. Feishu apps must subscribe to `vc.bot.meeting_invited_v1`; the docs were updated with that event. - Message delivery/session routing: covered. Invite-triggered replies use the real inviter DM target and avoid persisting a synthetic `vc-meeting:*` last-route target. - Tool compatibility: covered. The prompt instructs the agent to use `call_id` only when the available join tool supports it, keeping older `lark-cli` versions usable. - Security/privacy: no new credentials or persisted secrets. The handler keeps invite context limited to the fields needed for joining and reply routing. - Rollback: disable the Feishu event subscription or the bundled `feishu` channel/plugin to stop invite-triggered turns. ## Reviewer focus The remaining product decision is whether Feishu event subscription is sufficient opt-in for automatic meeting-join turns, or whether maintainers prefer an additional default-off Feishu config gate before merge.

target.title: fix(cli): guard plugins JSON.parse against malformed input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readJsonFile()` in `plugins-authoring-command.ts` calls `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(...))` without try-catch. If `package.json` or `openclaw.plugin.json` is malformed, the user gets a raw `SyntaxError` with no file path context, making it hard to diagnose which file is broken.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the same JSON.parse guard pattern that has been merged in 12+ community PRs (lsr911, solodmd, Pick-cat, etc.) — wrapping JSON.parse in try-catch with a descriptive error message that includes the file path.

## Evidence

**Before fix**: malformed `package.json` produces raw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ...` with no file context.

**After fix**: `Error: Malformed JSON in /path/to/package.json` with the original error preserved as `cause`.

**Test**: Added test "throws a user-friendly error when package.json is malformed JSON" — writes `{invalid json` to `package.json`, runs build command, verifies error message contains "Malformed JSON in".

```
✓ throws a user-friendly error when package.json is malformed JSON
```

## Merge Risk

Low. The change only wraps JSON.parse in try-catch; the error message uses the existing `formatOutputPath()` helper for consistent path formatting. Original error is preserved as `cause` for debugging.

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): treat blank env API keys as unconfigured
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` / `XI_API_KEY` environment values are truthy strings, so the ElevenLabs providers treated them as real credentials:

- `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured` returned `true` when `XI_API_KEY="  "`, so auto-selection could pick the realtime provider and only fail later at connection time.
- `transcribeElevenLabsAudio` skipped its `ElevenLabs API key missing` guard and sent the speech-to-text request with an empty `xi-api-key` header, surfacing as a confusing upstream 401 instead of a clear local configuration error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config-file key path already normalizes blanks (`normalizeResolvedSecretInputString`), and the profile fallback already trims (`resolveElevenLabsApiKeyWithProfileFallback`). Only the raw env fallbacks bypassed normalization. This routes them (plus the request-level key, matching the merged xAI handling in `realtime-transcription-provider.ts`) through the same shared `normalizeOptionalString` helper so blank values are treated as missing everywhere in this provider.

## Changes

- `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.ts`: `isConfigured` and `createSession` resolve the `XI_API_KEY` fallback via `normalizeOptionalString`, so whitespace-only values report unconfigured and session creation fails fast with `ElevenLabs API key missing`.
- `extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.ts`: the speech-to-text key resolution normalizes `req.apiKey`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, and `XI_API_KEY` with the same helper, so blank values are skipped and env keys are trimmed before being sent.
- Regression tests: whitespace-only env keys are treated as missing in both providers (including asserting no request is sent), and a padded env key is trimmed before use.

## User Impact

Operators with a whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`/`XI_API_KEY` (e.g., a placeholder left in an env file) now get a clear "ElevenLabs API key missing" error and the realtime provider correctly reports itself unconfigured, instead of a request sent with an empty credential that fails upstream. Real keys are unaffected (verified trimmed-to-same-value in tests). No config, migration, or API changes.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/elevenlabs/` — 38/38 passed on Node 22.22.0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` — no errors in changed files (only pre-existing `packages/net-policy` errors from a stale local dependency install).
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- Real HTTP proof below: loopback server + production functions, before/after this patch.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A whitespace-only `XI_API_KEY` made the realtime provider report configured, and the speech-to-text path sent a real request carrying an empty `xi-api-key` header instead of failing fast locally.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0, production functions imported directly from the changed sources, real `node:http` loopback server as the ElevenLabs API endpoint (`request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` to permit the loopback target). Current head: `446eea15d5535b6f0c64b2dca9c6d01047f43bac`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/elk-proof/proof.mts` with `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=""` and `XI_API_KEY="  "` in the environment. The driver starts a real HTTP server, calls `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured({ providerConfig: {} })`, then calls the production `transcribeElevenLabsAudio({ buffer, fileName, mime, baseUrl: <loopback>, request: { allowPrivateNetwork: true } })` and reads the server's received-request count and captured `xi-api-key` header back.

**Evidence after fix:** Before the patch (same driver, base revision): `isConfigured (whitespace XI_API_KEY): true`, `transcribeElevenLabsAudio outcome: resolved (request was sent)`, `server received requests: 1`, `captured xi-api-key header: ""`. target.title: fix(anthropic): complete transcript reverse-scan windows across short reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a Claude session transcript in the session catalog can fail with a
`Claude transcript changed while it was being read` error even when the file was
not touched.

`readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage` in `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.ts`
scans the transcript backwards in fixed windows. Each window was filled with a
single positional `handle.read(chunk, 0, size, position)` that then required
`bytesRead === size`, throwing otherwise. A positional read is allowed to return
fewer bytes than requested, so a benign short read tripped that check and failed
the transcript page with a message implying the file changed. The window is
in-bounds (`position` starts at `requestedEnd ≤ stat.size` and only decrements,
`size = min(chunk, position, …)`), so a short read there is not on its own a
reason to fail the page. The forward metadata scan in the same function already
completes short reads by looping; only this reverse scan threw.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reverse scan now fills each window across as many reads as it takes,
advancing both the buffer offset and the file position each read, so a benign
short read no longer surfaces a "transcript changed" error. A zero-byte read
before the window is filled is premature EOF, so that case still throws the same
error — only benign positive short reads stop failing the page. This is the same
loop the forward scan in this file already uses, and it follows the recently
merged short-read completion work (#108941, #108655, #108253) that had not
reached this plugin path; it is a different surface from #108242, which fills
bounded windows in the core gateway (`src/gateway/session-utils.fs.ts`).

## User Impact

No more spurious "Claude transcript changed while it was being read" failure when
paging Claude session transcripts. A zero-byte read before the window is filled
(premature EOF, consistent with the file being truncated or replaced mid-read)
still surfaces the same error.

## Evidence

Changed files: `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.ts` (reverse-scan fill
loop) and `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts` (two regression tests).

- `pages transcripts identically when every reverse-scan read returns short`:
  drives `readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage` through fault-injected short positional
  reads (each read capped to 4 KiB, so each 128 KiB window is completed across
  dozens of consecutive non-zero short reads) and asserts the paged
  items/order/cursor are identical to a normal read across two pages.
- `still reports a truncated transcript when a reverse-scan read hits EOF
  mid-window`: forces a zero-byte read mid-window and asserts the existing
  premature-EOF error is still raised.
- Before this fix the first test fails at the `bytesRead !== size` throw
  (production short reads cannot be induced deterministically, so mocked fault
  injection is the realistic deterministic proof for this failure class).
- `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts
  extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts`: 27 passed (25 existing + 2 new);
  before the fix: 1 failed | 26 passed. oxfmt and oxlint clean; extensions
  typecheck reports no errors in the changed files.

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

### Live Rollout Proof

I applied the same reset-queue behavior to two real `openclaw_gateway_1` runtimes that were on `2026.6.11`.

target.title: fix(agents): agent-created files get lowercased names on Windows
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, files and directories an agent creates get **lowercased names**. Ask for
`src/Components/MyComponent.tsx` and what lands on disk is `src\components\mycomponent.tsx`.

NTFS is case-insensitive but case-*preserving*, so nothing fails locally — the agent reads its own file
back fine. The damage shows up downstream: git records the lowercased name, and the TypeScript/React
import the agent just wrote (`./Components/MyComponent`) resolves on the author's Windows box but breaks
for every teammate on Linux/macOS and in CI. Any agent-authored name that is not already lowercase is
affected: `README.md`, `Dockerfile`, `MyClass.ts`.

For some names it is worse than a case change. `"İstanbul.md".toLowerCase()` is `"i̇stanbul.md"` —
U+0130 becomes the two code points U+0069 U+0307, one longer than the original and not reversible. So a
Turkish filename does not come back lowercased, it comes back **corrupted**.

This is Windows-only. The POSIX branch of the same function preserves case correctly today.

## Why This Change Was Made

`toRelativePathUnderRoot` (`src/agents/path-policy.ts:76-90`) ran both root and candidate through
`normalizeWindowsPathForComparison` and then **returned** the resulting relative path:

```ts
const rootForCompare = normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(rootResolved);
const targetForCompare = normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(resolvedCandidate);
const relative = path.win32.relative(rootForCompare, targetForCompare);
return validateRelativePathWithinBoundary({ relativePath: relative, ... });
```

That helper lowercases (`@openclaw/fs-safe@0.4.1`, `dist/path.js:17` →
`normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(...)`). Lowercasing is right for a **comparison key** — which is exactly
how the other two call sites use it — but this function hands the relative path back to callers, and they
build files out of it:

- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:1089-1092` — `mkdir`: `path.resolve(root, relative)` → `fs.mkdir`
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:1059-1060` — `writeWorkspaceFile` → `.write(relative, { mkdir: true })`
- `src/agents/apply-patch.ts:310,318,326` — `apply_patch` writeFile / remove / mkdirp

`toCanonicalRelativeWorkspacePath` (`agent-tools.read.ts:1167-1179`) does not rescue it: `fs.realpath`
restores the true case only of the **already-existing** ancestor, the new basename stays lowercased, and
line 1179 re-lowercases the whole thing on the way out. `assertSandboxPath` does not either — it is
handed the already-derived `resolved` path, not the original candidate.

The lowercasing was also never needed for the boundary math. `path.win32.relative` already matches the
root case-insensitively **and** returns the tail in its original case, so the pre-lowercasing bought
nothing and cost the filename. The one part of that normalization the boundary check does rely on is
extended-length prefix stripping — without it a `\\?\C:\...` candidate relativizes to
`..\..\..\?\C:\...` and gets rejected as an escape. So this adds `normalizeWindowsPathPreservingCase`
next to the comparison variant in `src/infra/path-guards.ts`. It mirrors that helper step for step —
including the trim — minus the lowercasing, and a test pins that equivalence directly so the two cannot
drift:

```ts
expect(normalizeWindowsPathPreservingCase(input).toLowerCase()).toBe(
  normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(input),
);
```

### Sibling surfaces

All three callers of `normalizeWindowsPathForComparison` were checked. Only this one was misusing it:

| Call site | Uses result as | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-record-reader.ts:215` | comparison key (`===`) | correct, untouched |
| `isPathInside` (fs-safe) | discards relative, returns boolean | correct, untouched |
| `src/agents/path-policy.ts` | **returns it to callers** | fixed here |

## Evidence

**Live before/after on real Windows** (Windows 11, NTFS, Turkish locale), driving the real
`toRelativeWorkspacePath` through the exact call pattern of `agent-tools.read.ts`, then reading the names
back with `fs.readdirSync`:

Before (`origin/main`):

```
--- case 1: agent asked for src\Components\MyComponent.tsx ---
  toRelativeWorkspacePath -> "src\components\mycomponent.tsx"
  ON DISK                 -> components/mycomponent.tsx

--- case 2: agent asked for İstanbul.md ---
  asked   : İstanbul.md  | length 11 | U+0130
  ON DISK : i̇stanbul.md | length 12 | U+0069 U+0307
  identical? NO  <- filename corrupted, not just lowercased
```

After (this branch):

```
--- case 1: agent asked for src\Components\MyComponent.tsx ---
  toRelativeWorkspacePath -> "src\Components\MyComponent.tsx"
  ON DISK                 -> Components/MyComponent.tsx

--- case 2: agent asked for İstanbul.md ---
  asked   : İstanbul.md | length 11 | U+0130
  ON DISK : İstanbul.md | length 11 | U+0130 U+0073
  identical? YES
```

**Why the existing test did not catch it:** `path-policy.test.ts:23` used an all-lowercase candidate
(`c:/users/user/openclaw/memory/log.txt`), which passes either way. The new cases use mixed case.

**Tests** — every added mixed-case assertion fails on `origin/main` and passes here:

```
path-policy.test.ts + path-guards.test.ts        41/41 passed
+ agent-tools.workspace-paths, apply-patch,
  installed-plugin-index-record-reader            111 passed | 12 skipped, 0 failed
max-lines ratchet                                 OK
dead-export ratchet (knip)                        0 entries
oxlint / oxfmt --check                            clean
tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json                        no errors in touched files
```

## Merge Risk

Low, but this touches a sandbox boundary, so here is the containment argument explicitly.

**The boundary decision is unchanged.** `path.win32.relative` compares case-insensitively, so
`relative(lower(a), lower(b))` and `relative(a, b)` return the same *structure* — same number of `..`
segments, same segment count, same absoluteness. Only the case of the returned characters differs.
`validateRelativePathWithinBoundary` looks at exactly that structure (`""`/`"."`, `".."`, `"../"`,
`"..\\"`, `isAbsolute`), so every accept/reject verdict is identical. Verified empirically:

```
root: C:\Users\User\OpenClaw
escape, no lowercasing        -> "..\Other\log.txt"     still rejected
root itself, differing case   -> ""                     allowRoot still honored
drive-letter case c: vs C:    -> "Memory\Log.txt"       still matched
\\?\ prefix NOT stripped      -> "..\..\..\?\C:\..."    why stripping is kept
```

Two of the added tests pin this directly — an escape that differs from the root only by case is still
rejected, and a differently-cased root still resolves to `""` under `allowRoot`. Both pass before and
after the change, which is the point.

Scope is one file's Windows branch plus one new helper with a single caller. POSIX behavior is untouched.

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(coding-agent): isolate Codex CLI CODEX_HOME from OpenClaw OAuth in skill launch forms
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users launching Codex workers from the bundled
`coding-agent` skill could reuse the ambient `~/.codex` ChatGPT OAuth state
that OpenClaw also depends on, which can leave one client failing with
`refresh_token_reused`.

Fixes #109704

## Why This Change Was Made

The manual Codex launch forms now require an authenticated `CODEX_HOME` outside
every Git worktree, and the scratch recipe logs in the isolated home before
running `codex exec`. The credential warning now matches Codex's supported
storage modes instead of implying that OAuth state is always in `auth.json`.

## User Impact

Users can run Codex background workers without placing Codex credentials in a
checkout or accidentally launching scratch workers from an empty auth store.

## Evidence

- Codex source inspection: `CODEX_HOME` selects the Codex home directory, and
  CLI auth may use file, keyring, or auto keyring-with-file-fallback storage
  (`codex-rs/utils/home-dir/src/lib.rs`, `codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs`,
  `codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs`, `codex-rs/login/src/server.rs`).
- Negative control: a fresh empty `CODEX_HOME` reports `Not logged in`, so the
  old scratch shape cannot complete an authenticated turn without login.
- Real scratch path: a temporary Git repo plus an authenticated external
  `CODEX_HOME` completed `codex exec` and returned the requested message.
- `pnpm docs:list`
- `git diff --check 5024c100a3244d605a7f874d3d48c842110f6a5c...HEAD`

```text
$ TMP_CODEX_HOME=$(mktemp -d); chmod 700 "$TMP_CODEX_HOME"; CODEX_HOME="$TMP_CODEX_HOME" codex login status
Not logged in

$ SCRATCH=$(mktemp -d); git -C "$SCRATCH" init
$ CODEX_HOME=<authenticated-external-home> codex login status
Logged in using ChatGPT
$ CODEX_HOME=<authenticated-external-home> codex exec --skip-git-repo-check -C <tmp-git-repo> --output-last-message <proof-output> 'Reply exactly: isolated-codex-home-ok'
workdir: <tmp-git-repo>
last_message:
isolated-codex-home-ok
```

AI-assisted: built with Codex

target.title: feat(bedrock): enable prompt caching for Nova models
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #29707. Amazon Nova generation models on Bedrock were still treated as unsupported non-Anthropic models, so OpenClaw forced `cacheRetention: "none"` and never emitted Bedrock `cachePoint` blocks for Nova requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

AWS documents explicit prompt caching support for Amazon Bedrock models, including Nova generation models: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html

This change teaches the Bedrock provider to recognize Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, Premier, and Nova 2 Lite refs, lets direct Nova requests keep their explicit cache settings, and keeps the existing no-cache fallback for unsupported non-Anthropic Bedrock models. For Nova, `cacheRetention: "long"` emits the default Bedrock cache point without reusing Claude's `ttl: "1h"` field.

Nova eligibility now has a single owner: the Amazon Bedrock provider normalization seam. The provider sets generic runtime compatibility metadata for eligible Nova models, while the shared agent cache-retention path only consumes that capability and contains no Bedrock model IDs or Nova-family matcher.

## User Impact

Users can enable prompt caching for Bedrock Nova text models without hitting the previous runtime no-cache override. Unsupported non-Anthropic Bedrock models, such as Mistral, continue to be protected from unsupported cache metadata.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1` on all 9 follow-up files
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint` on all 9 follow-up files
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-retention.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extra-params.cache-retention-default.test.ts` (38 tests passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/index.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` (100 tests passed)
- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts -t "uses provider-normalized model ids for OpenRouter transport"` (1 passed, 128 skipped)

- Fresh independent autoreview after addressing its integration-coverage finding: no actionable findings

The local extension and core-test `tsgo` lanes produced no diagnostics but exceeded 6-7 minute local timeouts. The corresponding GitHub checks are running on the pushed head.

Live Bedrock Nova request proof was not run because this contributor does not have a usable Nova-enabled AWS account. Redacted live `Converse` or `ConverseStream` proof showing accepted cache points and `cacheReadInputTokens` / `cacheWriteInputTokens` is still needed before merge.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): suppress fallback after route-matched message tool
target.body:
When heartbeat runs in message-tool-only mode, a successful generic message tool delivery can still be followed by duplicate free-text fallback narration in the same Telegram chat.

Fixes #84217

## Affected surface

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts`
  - Adds route-matched message tool delivery evidence for heartbeat replies only after the generic message tool sent to the same provider/target/account route.
- `src/auto-reply/reply-payload.ts`
  - Adds internal reply-payload metadata for route-scoped message tool delivery evidence.
- `src/auto-reply/heartbeat-reply-payload.ts`
  - Adds a heartbeat-specific evidence reader.
- `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts`
  - Suppresses free-text fallback only when the reply carries route-scoped message tool delivery evidence.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.ts`
  - Leaves heartbeat payloads available for heartbeat-specific route evidence instead of dropping them via generic message-tool dedupe first.
- Tests:
  - `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.tool-response.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`

## Scope

This is a parameter/evidence threading fix. It does not add a config flag, does not change heartbeat scheduling, and does not touch Slack identity, commitment, or channel-specific private paths.

The important semantic boundary is that "generic message tool delivery evidence" is not the same as "has outbound reply content". This PR only marks heartbeat replies when existing message-tool target evidence matches the same delivery route via the existing `resolveMessagingToolPayloadDedupe` route matcher. Global `messagingToolSentTexts` without route targets is intentionally not enough.

After Vincent's thread-route follow-up, I found one extra current-head issue while refreshing proof: generic reply-payload dedupe could drop the matched heartbeat payload before `heartbeat-runner` saw the route evidence. The current head keeps heartbeat payloads out of that generic dedupe layer so the heartbeat-specific suppression path receives the evidence and can still preserve no-route / wrong-topic fallback behavior.

## Prior art

Prior attempt #84273 was closed by contributor due to inability to provide live channel proof. This PR provides expanded source + runtime helper proof, with the helper semantic explicitly distinguishing "generic message tool delivery evidence" from "has outbound reply content" to address the message-delivery risk flagged in #84273.

The key difference from #84273 is route scope: #84273 marked heartbeat payloads after any message-tool send, while this PR only marks a heartbeat payload when committed `messagingToolSentTargets` match the reply route. If the message tool delivered to another route, or only global text evidence exists, heartbeat fallback still sends.

## Current-head P1 follow-up proof

This update addresses the ClawSweeper P1 finding "Suppress same-route fallback even when the text differs" on head `25958135ed2135dede29e716668ac34cfaea8007`.

The same-route heartbeat evidence rule now treats committed route-matched generic `message` tool target evidence as sufficient for a single plain heartbeat fallback payload, even when the fallback text differs from the tool body. Multi-payload heartbeat replies keep the existing text-match guard so unrelated fallback payloads are not suppressed. Rich payloads, media payloads, reasoning, no-route evidence, wrong-route evidence, and wrong-thread/topic evidence remain outside this suppression path.

## Current-head maintenance proof

After Vincent's route/thread follow-up moved this PR to `f21343bfd4`, CI exposed one current-head regression: `checks-node-auto-reply-reply-agent-runner` timed out in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.test.ts` at `dedupes duplicate same-target reply text without suppressing unrelated finals`.

Current head `df6f33925b` keeps the route/thread semantics from Vincent's follow-up, uses only the already-loaded channel registry for plugin-specific matching, and preserves internal route-string fallback for forms like `telegram:group:<chat>:topic:<thread>` without loading bundled channel implementations.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** heartbeat message-tool-only delivery should not send duplicate free-text fallback after the generic `message` tool has already delivered to the same route, but it must still send fallback when no same-route delivery evidence exists.
- **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw checkout on Linux, Node 22.22.2, pnpm 11.1.0, branch `wolf/heartbeat-suppress-after-message-tool`, head `14b8854108`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ran a local OpenClaw runtime helper that imports production `runHeartbeatOnce`, seeds a real `openclaw.json`-shaped config and session store, registers a local Telegram outbound adapter, then executes three heartbeat ticks: same-route evidence, no-route evidence, and wrong-thread/topic-unmarked evidence.
